# PR #57 / SFCC-89 — What's going on and what to do about it

**For the FED Lead · 22 Aug 2026**

PR #57, "PDP UI static product information." Written by Jhoan, not you. 30 files, +1702/−99.
Currently open, marked "changes requested," and blocked. Due 17 Aug — five days ago.

Nothing in the repo was changed to produce this. No commits, no pushes, nothing posted to the PR.

**How to read the confidence level.** Most of what follows I checked by running a command and
reading the output. Some of it comes from Jira, Confluence, Figma, or CI artifacts that I did not
re-run. Appendix A splits the two, item by item. Where something is a guess, it says so in the
sentence.

**One handling rule, no exceptions.** Four reference documents drove this analysis —
`uiBuild-knowledge.md`, `fedLead-playbook.md`, `fedBuild-manual.md`,
`zimmermann_frontend_lead_playbook.md`. They live outside the repo. **None of them can ever appear
in a PR comment, a commit message, a code comment, a Jira ticket, or Confluence.** Appendix B gives
you a citable repo source for every point you might need to raise. Where no repo source exists,
Appendix B says so — that's a gap to fill, not a citation to fudge.

---

## Start here

Ten lines. If you read nothing else:

1. **Merging this deletes add-to-bag from the live PDP.** Along with swatches, quantity picker,
   recommendations, accordions, 404 handling and the analytics hooks.
2. **The fix is deleting four lines.** Not a restructure. See §1.
3. **I found something bigger by accident: no page on this storefront server-renders. Anywhere.**
   Homepage, PDP, category, search, login — all return a loading spinner. Not this PR's fault.
   Pre-existing. This is the most important thing in the document. See §2.
4. **That also clears the reviewers.** "Nobody opened the preview" doesn't hold — opening it shows
   a spinner on every page, so it would have told them nothing.
5. **The component work is genuinely the best example of our styling pattern in the repo.** Keep it.
6. **Three of the "violations" in my earlier notes were wrong.** Acting on one of them would ship
   a layout bug. See §3.
7. **Ownership was already decided a month ago and nobody acted on it.** CODEOWNERS says Squad B.
8. **The one package this PR added is also the thing crashing the PDP.** Same object, two problems.
9. **Three of our own rules files are broken, missing, or teach a pattern that fails.** A developer
   following them literally ships a build error.
10. **This is not a hit piece.** A large share of what went wrong is ours, not Jhoan's. §5 splits it.

---

## Contents

- [1. If this merges tomorrow, here's what breaks](#1-if-this-merges-tomorrow-heres-what-breaks)

- [Appendix B — what to cite when you raise it](#appendix-b--what-to-cite-when-you-raise-it)

---

## 1. If this merges tomorrow, here's what breaks

### The headline

The live PDP loses add-to-bag, colour swatches, the quantity picker, recommended products, the
information accordions, wishlist, basket integration, proper 404 status codes, SSR cache headers,
deferred hydration, and all the Einstein / Data Cloud / Active Data analytics.

Not because anything was sabotaged. Because the new page renders three things — a grey box where
the gallery goes, the product info panel, and a breadcrumb — and it takes over the URL that used to
render Salesforce's 876-line page.

### Why it takes over, explained from scratch

PWA Kit has a file-replacement system. Put a file at `overrides/app/pages/foo.tsx` and it stands in
for the base Salesforce file at the same path. That's the whole idea, and it's how everything in
`overrides/` works.

The interesting part is *when* it kicks in. A webpack plugin inspects each import and only redirects
it if the import **names the package** — something like
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/breadcrumb`. Its own code comment says it plainly:

> *"returns true only if the import request points to a package in 'extends'… If false, the import
> request proceeds to the base package in node_modules"*

Now look at how base Salesforce loads its own PDP:

```js
const ProductDetail = loadable(() => import('./pages/product-detail'), {fallback})
```

That's a **relative** path. No package name. So it is never redirected — base Salesforce keeps
loading its own real page, untouched.

So why does the storefront show the cut-down version? Because of this, in `overrides/app/routes.tsx`:

```js
{
  path: '/product/:productId',
  component: ProductDetail,     // ← the override
},
..._routes,                     // ← base Salesforce's routes, including the real PDP
```

Our route is registered **first**. First match wins. That's the entire mechanism.

**Delete lines 37–40 of `overrides/app/routes.tsx` and the full base PDP is back.** I confirmed both
pages are sitting in the shipped bundle side by side — `build/pages-product-detail.js` contains
markers unique to our override *and* markers unique to the base page, and the same file fetched from
the live preview is byte-for-byte identical to my local build.

**Why this matters for planning:** earlier notes (mine included) said there were *two* mechanisms
doing this and that deleting the route wouldn't help. That was wrong, and it inflated the fix from
four lines to a rewrite. The regression and the delivery are now separate problems, which is a much
better position to be in.

### The breadcrumb is the opposite case, and it really is a problem

Same system, different outcome. Two base Salesforce files import the breadcrumb **by package name**:

- `product-view/index.jsx:45`
- `product-list/partials/page-header.jsx:14`

Package name means the redirect fires. So both of those now get our breadcrumb. The second one is
the **PLP**.

A PDP ticket has silently restyled the product listing page — chevron separator replaced with `/`,
uppercase, the `useStyleConfig('Breadcrumb')` hook orphaned, the `sf-crumb-item` test id gone. Squad
B's page changed appearance with no design review and no notice. Nobody would find this except QA or
a shopper.

There's a second-order oddity worth flagging to Squad B: SFCC-89's AC puts the breadcrumb *below*
the product images. On the PLP, breadcrumbs are top-of-page wayfinding. The same component may not
want the same placement.

---

## 2. The bigger problem I found by accident

**No page on this storefront is server-rendered. On any route. On any environment I could reach.**

I went looking for the reported PDP crash on the preview environment and found something else: every
URL returns HTTP 200 with the app shell rendered and a **loading spinner** where the page content
should be.

| URL | Result |
|---|---|
| preview `/` | 200, spinner |
| preview `/en-au/product/8637DS241-3` | 200, spinner |
| preview `/en-au/product/DEFINITELY-NOT-A-SKU` | 200, spinner |
| preview `/en-au/category/womens` | 200, spinner |
| preview `/en-au/search?q=dress` | 200, spinner |
| preview `/en-au/login` | 200, spinner |
| **`test` tier `/`** | 200, spinner |
| **`test` tier `/en-au/category/womens`** | 200, spinner |

Supporting detail: the PDP's HTML is identical to the homepage's apart from the canonical URL. Its
`<title>` is `Retail React App` — the fallback, not a product name. The strings `Style Code` and
`Unable to load product information` appear **zero** times in the served HTML. Same output for curl,
for a real Chrome user-agent, and for Googlebot. The shell itself *is* server-rendered — header,
footer, the SVG sprite, the full theme. It's the page components that never arrive.

And the preview genuinely is running this PR's code — the served chunk matches my local build byte
for byte.

**What this costs.** The project brief opens with *"Must be robust and secure and SEO-friendly"* and
sets a ≤2s p75 mobile LCP budget. Client-rendered spinners defeat both. Every "compare the preview
against Figma" review anyone has ever done on this project has been reviewing a client-rendered page.

**My best guess at the cause, stated as a guess.** Every page in base Salesforce's route table is
wrapped in `loadable(() => import(...), {fallback})`. A correct shell plus a spinner in `<main>` is
exactly what you get when the server-side chunk resolution doesn't happen and the `fallback` renders
instead. That points at `ChunkExtractor` / `loadable-stats.json` wiring in `overrides/app/ssr.js`
and `overrides/app/ssr/` — **Tier 1, Integration-owned, and one of the four absolutely-untouchable
files.** Do not go near it. Report it.

**Two things this changes immediately.**

First, it clears the reviewers. The criticism that nobody opened the preview URL doesn't survive:
opening it shows a spinner on the PDP *and* on the homepage, indistinguishable. Any reviewer who
looked would reasonably conclude "previews don't SSR here" and move on. Don't use that as a stick.

Second, the reported PDP crash and this finding are consistent, not contradictory. The crash happens
where SSR actually evaluates the page module — which is where the CI Playwright run served from. On
MRT it's **masked**, because MRT never evaluates the page module server-side at all. Which also
means: **the MRT preview is not a usable SSR smoke test on this project.** Any process fix that says
"hit the preview and check the status code" would have produced a false pass here.

**One gap before you escalate.** I could only reach the preview and the `test` tier — `test`
publishes its URL as an environment variable, `dev` and `sit` don't, and I had no URL for `staging`
or `prod`. Find out whether they behave the same before deciding how loud to be.

---

## 3. Corrections — including to my own earlier notes

Trust matters more than looking consistent, so these are stated flatly.

### Don't "fix" three of the flagged styling violations — you'd ship a bug

I earlier told you nine `var(--zimm-*)` uses in component files were all violations to move into
theme recipes. **Three of them are correct as written.**

Here's why. Chakra resolves style props against named scales in the theme, but our
`overrides/app/theme/index.ts` only registers six of them: `borderWidths`, `breakpoints`, `colors`,
`fonts`, `space`, `textStyles`. **`sizes` is not registered.** So a bare token key works fine on
`margin` or `padding` (which resolve through `space`) and silently misresolves on `width`, `height`
or `boxSize` (which resolve through `sizes`).

Lines 69–71 of the page are `<Skeleton height="var(--zimm-scale-800)" />` and similar. `height` is
a sizing prop. The raw `var()` is the **only** correct form there. Convert them to bare keys and the
skeletons break.

Worth noting Jhoan got this exactly right — the same lines use `mb="m"` and `mb="xl"`, bare keys on
a *spacing* prop, which is correct. He wasn't guessing.

The revised picture:

| Site | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `product-detail:69, 70, 71` — `Skeleton height` | **Correct. Leave alone.** |
| `product-detail:63` — `pt` 16px | Real violation, `m` exists, safe to move |
| `product-detail:61, 62` (base) — 32px gutter | Real violation, but the right value is **30px**, not the 32px `2xl` token. Use `grid.containerPadding.base`. |
| `product-detail:52` — `columnGap` 180px | Real, but **no named token exists** — our spacing scale tops out at 160px. Designer question. |
| `product-detail:62` (md) — `pr` 140px | Same. Designer question. |
| `breadcrumb:33`, `zimmPageToolbar:58` | **Different problem entirely** — these are motion values, and there's no motion scale to reach for. Import the `motion` constant from `app/theme/foundation`. Heads up: `motion.ts` says its own values are *"PROVISIONAL… Do not treat as final."* |

### I was wrong about the fonts

I told you a Tier 1 governance file was factually wrong about self-hosted fonts. It isn't. On this
branch and on `develop`, `frozenFiles.md` says **"No font binaries in this repo"** and explains that
type renders from the fallback stack — which is correct, and is a licence position, not an oversight.

The "fonts are self-hosted" wording exists only on the SFCC-55 footer branch. **My session started
on that branch**, so the copy of the rules in my context was that branch's version, and it didn't
update when I switched. Practical takeaway for you: anything I quote from `.claude/rules/` is worth
re-checking against the branch actually in hand.

The downstream conclusion survives and still matters: there are no font files, so every local and
preview visual check rendered the fallback face. **No type metric on this PR has ever been visually
validated** — and SFCC-732/733 are the styling ACs that will be QA'd on exactly those metrics.

*Related risk:* if the SFCC-55 branch merges, it brings a `frozenFiles.md` that asserts self-hosted
fonts plus two `.woff2` files — which would contradict the Monotype licence position currently
recorded in that same Tier 1 file. Flag it to whoever owns SFCC-55 before it lands.

### The jsdom / bundle-budget link doesn't exist

Several notes connected the new dependency to `vendor.js` sitting at 95.4% of its budget. There's no
connection. `grep -c jsdom build/vendor.js` returns **0**. The package ships a browser entry point
that doesn't import jsdom at all, and the client build resolves to it. Client-side cost is
`dompurify` alone.

The 95.4% is real and is a standing risk with ~25 kB of headroom — but it's pre-existing and
unrelated. **Raise them separately or the budget concern gets dismissed along with the dependency.**

This also improves the options: because a jsdom-free browser entry exists, "rip the package out"
isn't the only route. See §6.

### SEO needs no new package

An unresolved CodeRabbit thread asks for `react-helmet`, and I'd previously called that a Hard Rule
#7 problem. It isn't — **`react-helmet@6.1.0` is already installed** as a dependency of
`retail-react-app`, and base ships a ready-made `app/components/seo` wrapper. Import that. It's a
published entrypoint, so it satisfies our import rules too.

One thing that comes with it: the base SEO block reads `product.pageTitle` and `pageMetaTags`, and
our `useProduct` call requests no `expand` list at all where base requests nine fields plus
`perPricebook: true`. Restoring SEO means restoring the expand list.

**Which raises a question nobody has asked.** AC-2 wants a single full price. The override reads
`product.price` with no `perPricebook` and no `expand: ['prices']`. I haven't proved that returns
the wrong number — but the base page doesn't trust that field, and neither should we without
checking against live data.

### A few smaller ones

- **A bare `Breadcrumb` theme recipe would be a trap.** Base Salesforce registers its own
  `Breadcrumb` recipe, so `extendTheme` would deep-merge ours into theirs — the exact failure that
  cost you time on the footer. Name it `ZimmBreadcrumb`.
- **The focus ring is inconsistent, not absent.** `zimmPageToolbar` applies a
  `.zimm-focus-visible` class that does express `_focusVisible` properly, so that control is fine.
  The **breadcrumb has no focus treatment at all** — and it's the interactive element the AC
  requires. Browsers still paint a default outline, so this is a consistency defect, **not** a WCAG
  failure. Don't over-claim it. The real finding is that one PR answers the same question three
  different ways.
- **Lint:** 22 errors repo-wide, **5 of them this branch's**, and eslint reports 21 of 22 as
  auto-fixable. The one it flags as not auto-fixable sits on the same line as a prettier fix that
  removes the same character, so `lint:fix` should clear all five. Verify after running. Don't fold
  in the 17 pre-existing errors in the Contentful definitions file.
- **`auditTokenUsage.mjs` doesn't exist**, and the rule mandating it is
  `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` — a repo file. That's good news: it's citable, so fixing it is
  normal work.
- **Three Figma node IDs are in circulation** — the tickets cite `5804-170721`, the measurements
  came from `5083:70358`, the page node is `3087:15747`. Don't assume they're the same frame. Confirm
  with the BA before QA measures against the wrong one.
- **The PR body and CI disagree on test results** — the body says 4 of 9 scenarios run and pass, CI
  says 0 of 7 with 2 skipped. I didn't re-run Playwright. Treat the body as a claim and CI as an
  observation, and re-run before quoting either.

---

## 4. What this PR gets genuinely right

Read this before §5, because the calibration matters.

**The component and its theme recipe are the best worked example of our styling pattern anywhere in
this repo.** `ZimmPdpProductInfo` is correctly namespaced so `extendTheme` has nothing to merge into.
It's registered properly. All five of its parts are actually consumed — not a registered-but-unread
recipe. The two escape hatches it needs are exported *from the theme file* and imported by the
component, so even the call-site styling is named where styling belongs, with a written note
explaining what would collapse them and why that's blocked. **Copy this shape for everything else.**

single most dangerous trap in this codebase and the branch is completely clean on it. Given that a

---

## 1. If this merges tomorrow, here's what breaks

### The headline

The live PDP loses add-to-bag, colour swatches, the quantity picker, recommended products, the
information accordions, wishlist, basket integration, proper 404 status codes, SSR cache headers,
deferred hydration, and all the Einstein / Data Cloud / Active Data analytics.

Not because anything was sabotaged. Because the new page renders three things — a grey box where
the gallery goes, the product info panel, and a breadcrumb — and it takes over the URL that used to
render Salesforce's 876-line page.

### Why it takes over, explained from scratch

PWA Kit has a file-replacement system. Put a file at `overrides/app/pages/foo.tsx` and it stands in
for the base Salesforce file at the same path. That's the whole idea, and it's how everything in
`overrides/` works.

The interesting part is *when* it kicks in. A webpack plugin inspects each import and only redirects
it if the import **names the package** — something like
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/breadcrumb`. Its own code comment says it plainly:

> *"returns true only if the import request points to a package in 'extends'… If false, the import
> request proceeds to the base package in node_modules"*

Now look at how base Salesforce loads its own PDP:

```js
const ProductDetail = loadable(() => import('./pages/product-detail'), {fallback})
```

That's a **relative** path. No package name. So it is never redirected — base Salesforce keeps
loading its own real page, untouched.

So why does the storefront show the cut-down version? Because of this, in `overrides/app/routes.tsx`:

```js
{
  path: '/product/:productId',
  component: ProductDetail,     // ← the override
},
..._routes,                     // ← base Salesforce's routes, including the real PDP
```

Our route is registered **first**. First match wins. That's the entire mechanism.

**Delete lines 37–40 of `overrides/app/routes.tsx` and the full base PDP is back.** I confirmed both
pages are sitting in the shipped bundle side by side — `build/pages-product-detail.js` contains
markers unique to our override *and* markers unique to the base page, and the same file fetched from
the live preview is byte-for-byte identical to my local build.

**Why this matters for planning:** earlier notes (mine included) said there were *two* mechanisms
doing this and that deleting the route wouldn't help. That was wrong, and it inflated the fix from
four lines to a rewrite. The regression and the delivery are now separate problems, which is a much
better position to be in.

### The breadcrumb is the opposite case, and it really is a problem

Same system, different outcome. Two base Salesforce files import the breadcrumb **by package name**:

- `product-view/index.jsx:45`
- `product-list/partials/page-header.jsx:14`

Package name means the redirect fires. So both of those now get our breadcrumb. The second one is
the **PLP**.

A PDP ticket has silently restyled the product listing page — chevron separator replaced with `/`,
uppercase, the `useStyleConfig('Breadcrumb')` hook orphaned, the `sf-crumb-item` test id gone. Squad
B's page changed appearance with no design review and no notice. Nobody would find this except QA or
a shopper.

There's a second-order oddity worth flagging to Squad B: SFCC-89's AC puts the breadcrumb *below*
the product images. On the PLP, breadcrumbs are top-of-page wayfinding. The same component may not
want the same placement.

---

## 2. The bigger problem I found by accident

**No page on this storefront is server-rendered. On any route. On any environment I could reach.**

I went looking for the reported PDP crash on the preview environment and found something else: every
URL returns HTTP 200 with the app shell rendered and a **loading spinner** where the page content
should be.

| URL | Result |
|---|---|
| preview `/` | 200, spinner |
| preview `/en-au/product/8637DS241-3` | 200, spinner |
| preview `/en-au/product/DEFINITELY-NOT-A-SKU` | 200, spinner |
| preview `/en-au/category/womens` | 200, spinner |
| preview `/en-au/search?q=dress` | 200, spinner |
| preview `/en-au/login` | 200, spinner |
| **`test` tier `/`** | 200, spinner |
| **`test` tier `/en-au/category/womens`** | 200, spinner |

Supporting detail: the PDP's HTML is identical to the homepage's apart from the canonical URL. Its
`<title>` is `Retail React App` — the fallback, not a product name. The strings `Style Code` and
`Unable to load product information` appear **zero** times in the served HTML. Same output for curl,
for a real Chrome user-agent, and for Googlebot. The shell itself *is* server-rendered — header,
footer, the SVG sprite, the full theme. It's the page components that never arrive.

And the preview genuinely is running this PR's code — the served chunk matches my local build byte
for byte.

**What this costs.** The project brief opens with *"Must be robust and secure and SEO-friendly"* and
sets a ≤2s p75 mobile LCP budget. Client-rendered spinners defeat both. Every "compare the preview
against Figma" review anyone has ever done on this project has been reviewing a client-rendered page.

**My best guess at the cause, stated as a guess.** Every page in base Salesforce's route table is
wrapped in `loadable(() => import(...), {fallback})`. A correct shell plus a spinner in `<main>` is
exactly what you get when the server-side chunk resolution doesn't happen and the `fallback` renders
instead. That points at `ChunkExtractor` / `loadable-stats.json` wiring in `overrides/app/ssr.js`
and `overrides/app/ssr/` — **Tier 1, Integration-owned, and one of the four absolutely-untouchable
files.** Do not go near it. Report it.

**Two things this changes immediately.**

First, it clears the reviewers. The criticism that nobody opened the preview URL doesn't survive:
opening it shows a spinner on the PDP *and* on the homepage, indistinguishable. Any reviewer who
looked would reasonably conclude "previews don't SSR here" and move on. Don't use that as a stick.

Second, the reported PDP crash and this finding are consistent, not contradictory. The crash happens
where SSR actually evaluates the page module — which is where the CI Playwright run served from. On
MRT it's **masked**, because MRT never evaluates the page module server-side at all. Which also
means: **the MRT preview is not a usable SSR smoke test on this project.** Any process fix that says
"hit the preview and check the status code" would have produced a false pass here.

**One gap before you escalate.** I could only reach the preview and the `test` tier — `test`
publishes its URL as an environment variable, `dev` and `sit` don't, and I had no URL for `staging`
or `prod`. Find out whether they behave the same before deciding how loud to be.

---

## 3. Corrections — including to my own earlier notes

Trust matters more than looking consistent, so these are stated flatly.

### Don't "fix" three of the flagged styling violations — you'd ship a bug

I earlier told you nine `var(--zimm-*)` uses in component files were all violations to move into
theme recipes. **Three of them are correct as written.**

Here's why. Chakra resolves style props against named scales in the theme, but our
`overrides/app/theme/index.ts` only registers six of them: `borderWidths`, `breakpoints`, `colors`,
`fonts`, `space`, `textStyles`. **`sizes` is not registered.** So a bare token key works fine on
`margin` or `padding` (which resolve through `space`) and silently misresolves on `width`, `height`
or `boxSize` (which resolve through `sizes`).

Lines 69–71 of the page are `<Skeleton height="var(--zimm-scale-800)" />` and similar. `height` is
a sizing prop. The raw `var()` is the **only** correct form there. Convert them to bare keys and the
skeletons break.

Worth noting Jhoan got this exactly right — the same lines use `mb="m"` and `mb="xl"`, bare keys on
a *spacing* prop, which is correct. He wasn't guessing.

The revised picture:

| Site | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `product-detail:69, 70, 71` — `Skeleton height` | **Correct. Leave alone.** |
| `product-detail:63` — `pt` 16px | Real violation, `m` exists, safe to move |
| `product-detail:61, 62` (base) — 32px gutter | Real violation, but the right value is **30px**, not the 32px `2xl` token. Use `grid.containerPadding.base`. |
| `product-detail:52` — `columnGap` 180px | Real, but **no named token exists** — our spacing scale tops out at 160px. Designer question. |
| `product-detail:62` (md) — `pr` 140px | Same. Designer question. |
| `breadcrumb:33`, `zimmPageToolbar:58` | **Different problem entirely** — these are motion values, and there's no motion scale to reach for. Import the `motion` constant from `app/theme/foundation`. Heads up: `motion.ts` says its own values are *"PROVISIONAL… Do not treat as final."* |

### I was wrong about the fonts

I told you a Tier 1 governance file was factually wrong about self-hosted fonts. It isn't. On this
branch and on `develop`, `frozenFiles.md` says **"No font binaries in this repo"** and explains that
type renders from the fallback stack — which is correct, and is a licence position, not an oversight.

The "fonts are self-hosted" wording exists only on the SFCC-55 footer branch. **My session started
on that branch**, so the copy of the rules in my context was that branch's version, and it didn't
update when I switched. Practical takeaway for you: anything I quote from `.claude/rules/` is worth
re-checking against the branch actually in hand.

The downstream conclusion survives and still matters: there are no font files, so every local and
preview visual check rendered the fallback face. **No type metric on this PR has ever been visually
validated** — and SFCC-732/733 are the styling ACs that will be QA'd on exactly those metrics.

*Related risk:* if the SFCC-55 branch merges, it brings a `frozenFiles.md` that asserts self-hosted
fonts plus two `.woff2` files — which would contradict the Monotype licence position currently
recorded in that same Tier 1 file. Flag it to whoever owns SFCC-55 before it lands.

### The jsdom / bundle-budget link doesn't exist

Several notes connected the new dependency to `vendor.js` sitting at 95.4% of its budget. There's no
connection. `grep -c jsdom build/vendor.js` returns **0**. The package ships a browser entry point
that doesn't import jsdom at all, and the client build resolves to it. Client-side cost is
`dompurify` alone.

The 95.4% is real and is a standing risk with ~25 kB of headroom — but it's pre-existing and
unrelated. **Raise them separately or the budget concern gets dismissed along with the dependency.**

This also improves the options: because a jsdom-free browser entry exists, "rip the package out"
isn't the only route. See §6.

### SEO needs no new package

An unresolved CodeRabbit thread asks for `react-helmet`, and I'd previously called that a Hard Rule
#7 problem. It isn't — **`react-helmet@6.1.0` is already installed** as a dependency of
`retail-react-app`, and base ships a ready-made `app/components/seo` wrapper. Import that. It's a
published entrypoint, so it satisfies our import rules too.

One thing that comes with it: the base SEO block reads `product.pageTitle` and `pageMetaTags`, and
our `useProduct` call requests no `expand` list at all where base requests nine fields plus
`perPricebook: true`. Restoring SEO means restoring the expand list.

**Which raises a question nobody has asked.** AC-2 wants a single full price. The override reads
`product.price` with no `perPricebook` and no `expand: ['prices']`. I haven't proved that returns
the wrong number — but the base page doesn't trust that field, and neither should we without
checking against live data.

### A few smaller ones

- **A bare `Breadcrumb` theme recipe would be a trap.** Base Salesforce registers its own
  `Breadcrumb` recipe, so `extendTheme` would deep-merge ours into theirs — the exact failure that
  cost you time on the footer. Name it `ZimmBreadcrumb`.
- **The focus ring is inconsistent, not absent.** `zimmPageToolbar` applies a
  `.zimm-focus-visible` class that does express `_focusVisible` properly, so that control is fine.
  The **breadcrumb has no focus treatment at all** — and it's the interactive element the AC
  requires. Browsers still paint a default outline, so this is a consistency defect, **not** a WCAG
  failure. Don't over-claim it. The real finding is that one PR answers the same question three
  different ways.
- **Lint:** 22 errors repo-wide, **5 of them this branch's**, and eslint reports 21 of 22 as
  auto-fixable. The one it flags as not auto-fixable sits on the same line as a prettier fix that
  removes the same character, so `lint:fix` should clear all five. Verify after running. Don't fold
  in the 17 pre-existing errors in the Contentful definitions file.
- **`auditTokenUsage.mjs` doesn't exist**, and the rule mandating it is
  `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` — a repo file. That's good news: it's citable, so fixing it is
  normal work.
- **Three Figma node IDs are in circulation** — the tickets cite `5804-170721`, the measurements
  came from `5083:70358`, the page node is `3087:15747`. Don't assume they're the same frame. Confirm
  with the BA before QA measures against the wrong one.
- **The PR body and CI disagree on test results** — the body says 4 of 9 scenarios run and pass, CI
  says 0 of 7 with 2 skipped. I didn't re-run Playwright. Treat the body as a claim and CI as an
  observation, and re-run before quoting either.

---

## 4. What this PR gets genuinely right

Read this before §5, because the calibration matters.

**The component and its theme recipe are the best worked example of our styling pattern anywhere in
this repo.** `ZimmPdpProductInfo` is correctly namespaced so `extendTheme` has nothing to merge into.
It's registered properly. All five of its parts are actually consumed — not a registered-but-unread
recipe. The two escape hatches it needs are exported *from the theme file* and imported by the
component, so even the call-site styling is named where styling belongs, with a written note
explaining what would collapse them and why that's blocked. **Copy this shape for everything else.**

**Zero bare scale keys on any sizing or typography prop, across the entire branch.** This is the
single most dangerous trap in this codebase and the branch is completely clean on it. Given that a
mistake here fails silently, that's not luck.

**The provisional column width was flagged in code as provisional** rather than silently guessed.
The value turned out to be wrong — 218px measured against 360px written — but the *behaviour* was
exactly right, and that distinction is the whole point of the rule.

**Accessibility is asserted, not claimed.** Proper `h1`, `nav[aria-label]`/`ol`/`li`, `aria-current`,
`aria-hidden` on separators, and a Storybook `play` that proves the *negative* case when content is
absent. Storybook a11y is gated at `error` in CI, so those assertions genuinely run.

**Also right:** data fetching lives only in the page, all three components are pure and prop-driven ·
`getTemplateName` retained, easy to drop · a discriminated union for the toolbar props, exactly per
our TypeScript rules · both `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` sites sanitised — the security instinct was
right, only the dependency was wrong · `storybook/test` imported correctly *against* a repo rule that
says otherwise · Storybook categorisation right four times out of four · gherkin-first followed, the
`.feature` file exists · `tsc` clean, Vitest 146/146, Storybook 27/27 · **and every Tier 1 file left
alone** — no workflows, no playwright config, no `.storybook/`, no theme foundation, no `ssr.js`. On
an overdue story with three tempting Tier 1 shortcuts sitting right there, that's discipline.

---

## 5. What went wrong, and how much of it is ours

### Ours

Name these out loud so Jhoan isn't reviewed for them.

1. **Five reviewer teams were asked on 18 Aug. Four days later, none had responded.** Every one of
   the 8 reviews on this PR is CodeRabbit. The "changes requested" status blocking it is a bot's.
   There is no review SLA anywhere and no escalation path.
2. **The review tool can't detect what we ask it to detect.** The preview shows a spinner on every
   route (§2). Blaming reviewers for not opening a URL that would have told them nothing is the
   wrong correction — the right one is that we didn't know our own preview doesn't SSR.
3. **Three of our rules files are broken, missing, or teach a failing pattern.**
   `overrideStyling.md` mandates a script that doesn't exist, and cross-references
   `.claude/rules/overrides.md` — which **isn't on `develop`**. That missing file is precisely the
   one containing the override pre-flight checklist and the grep that would have caught the PLP
   regression. And `testing.md:87` tells developers to
   `import {expect, userEvent, within} from '@storybook/test'` — **a package that does not exist**
   on our installed Storybook. Jhoan ignored the rule and imported correctly. Anyone who followed it
   literally would have shipped a module-not-found.
4. **`eslint`, `prettier` and `tsc --noEmit` are gated by nothing.** Not CI, not a hook, not a
   stated team expectation. The check that would have caught those 5 lint errors doesn't exist in
   any form.
5. **"Build it in Storybook" is structurally impossible for a page here.** A page calls
   `useProduct`, which needs a `CommerceApiProvider`, and the only place to add one is
   `.storybook/preview.tsx` — Tier 1, frozen. The duplicated page JSX in the story is a **cornered
   outcome, not laziness**, and he wrote down the reason.
6. **The `ui-kits` convention he followed has no repo rule on `develop`.** He placed one component
   inside `ui-kits/` and one outside it, and **nobody can tell him which is right from a source he
   can point at.**
7. **The design isn't locked and the story was already late.** Confluence puts PDP stories
   ready-for-development on **24 Aug**; the story was due **17 Aug**. He was asked to build against
   an unlocked design on a deadline that had already passed.
8. **Type metrics were never measurable locally** — no font binaries, by licence. The "tested
   locally" checkbox could not have validated a single type metric, which is what SFCC-732/733 will
   be QA'd on.
9. **`sprintScope.md` is stale** — self-labelled draft, says "Sprint 0 in progress," dates Sprint 3
   wrongly — while Hard Rule #14 binds developers to it.
10. **The Squad A/B ownership contradiction was written down on 9 July and left open.** It's now the
    reason a real PR can't be routed to the right reviewer.

### His

Same standard, no inflation.

1. **The Tier 1 dependency.** The PR body names the gate verbatim — *"needs integration team
   approval (Hard Rule #7)"* — and the package was added anyway. Spotting a gate and then crossing
   it is a different failure from not knowing it exists. Worth a direct question rather than a
   comment restating the rule: what unblocked it — a verbal OK, time pressure, or an assumption the
   PR gate would catch it?
2. **Copy-first wasn't done on either shadowed module.** No `[overrides]` marker was ever committed;
   the breadcrumb was written from scratch at 71 lines against a 67-line base with a different
   implementation, and the page at 48 lines against 876. **This one omission is the root cause of
   both the PDP capability loss and the PLP regression.**
3. **The bridge-pattern grep wasn't run.** One command, and it returns two lines. Mitigating: the
   rules file spelling out that procedure doesn't exist on `develop`.
4. **The PR body is stale in five ways** — says the dependency isn't added when it is; lists 15 of
   30 files and omits every Tier 1 file; names a path that doesn't exist; ticks "lint passes"; tiers
   the page as Squad A against CODEOWNERS.
5. **Diagnosis by proxy.** The body blames sandbox provisioning for the Playwright failures. That
   explains *some* skips, not every `/product/*` request failing on valid and invalid SKUs alike.
   When a check returns zero, establish which zero it is.
6. **`npm start` was run**, self-reported, against an explicit "Do not run."
7. **The migration stopped one commit short.** `3e1686b` built the recipe correctly; the very next
   and final commit edited a padding **constant** instead of creating the second recipe. Mitigating:
   that constant uses correct named keys and carries a comment explaining its derivation. It's
   orderly, traceable code sitting one level too low. **Finish it, don't restart it.**
8. **Requirements defects** — `product.id` used as style code where it should be the master style
   number; `c_sizeFit` scraped for model copy where SFCC-26 created `modelFit` for exactly that;
   `shortDescription || longDescription` as a guess; and a regex that only matches a bare `<li>` and
   only the English string, so the model line vanishes on 10 of 11 locales. Partly forced — SFCC-26
   hasn't reached the sandbox he tests against, so the right field may genuinely not exist there.
   Ask before charging it.

**The line to use in the regroup:** the component layer is the best example of our styling pattern in
the repo and should be carried forward almost verbatim. The integration layer reproduces, one for
one, the failures the skipped pre-flight steps exist to prevent — and three of those steps are
documented in files that are broken, missing, or wrong.

Deleting those four lines restores the base page. This is verified — treat it as fact.

Look at what the base page composes — especially `product-view` — and work out whether the SFCC-89 static info (name, price, description, style code, model copy) naturally belongs inside an override of `product-view` or one of the base page's `partials/` rather than the page itself. Repo: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa`, branch `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-ui-static-product-information` @ `d526ad1`.

## The question, in the Lead's own words

"Based on the user story, the figma design, and what we have in the PR #55 for the footer, what are the atoms, molecules, organisms for these components? What is to be built from scratch? What is to be reused? What is for overriding? What is custom and not out-of-the-box?"

The team works **atom-first**: build atoms, compose into molecules, then organisms, then pages. Out-of-the-box (OOTB) Salesforce parts stay OOTB until their own ticket lands.

## Your three inputs — read ALL of them

**1. The user story (SFCC-89) and the Figma spec.** Both are already captured. Read:
- `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/4447dd18-bbe0-4a85-aae2-6e8935bf7947/scratchpad/req-jira.md` — the ticket, its six acceptance criteria, and the explicit in/out of scope lists
- `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/4447dd18-bbe0-4a85-aae2-6e8935bf7947/scratchpad/req-figma.md` — the measured design spec, including which text styles / colour tokens / spacing values map to existing repo tokens and which are gaps
- Also `conventions.md` and `code-state.md` in that same folder for what already exists

**2. The footer precedent — PR #55.** This is the reference implementation the Lead wants matched. It is on the local branch `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui`. Do NOT check that branch out. Read it with git, e.g.:
- `git ls-tree -r --name-only feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui -- overrides/app/components overrides/app/theme/components`
- `git show feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui:<path>` for each interesting file
Work out the ACTUAL established pattern from the code: how are atoms/molecules/organisms laid out, how is styling done (theme recipe naming, registration), what naming conventions, what gets a story, what gets a test, how are shared/OOTB components consumed vs overridden. Note the `Zimm` prefix convention on theme recipes and WHY it exists (base SFCC recipes deep-merge via `extendTheme` if the key collides).

**3. What exists in the repo today.** Verify, do not assume:
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` — what is actually in it on this branch
- `overrides/app/components/` — the full list
- `overrides/app/theme/components/` — which recipes exist and are registered in `index.ts`
- Which PDP-adjacent SFCC components have overrides and which do not (`image-gallery`, `swatch-group`, `display-price`, `product-view`, `quantity-picker`, `breadcrumb`, `product-tile`)
- What base SFCC ships that could be reused instead of built: check `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` for anything relevant, and `app/components/shared/ui` (note: 103 relative re-exports, 212 base files import the barrel, 0 import deep paths — so overriding `shared/ui/<Name>` intercepts nothing)

## What to produce

**A decomposition table** covering every UI element in SFCC-89's scope (product name, price, description, style code, model copy, breadcrumb — plus the page-level layout/grid). For each row:

| Element | Tier (atom/molecule/organism/page) | Verdict | Why | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Where **Verdict** is exactly one of: **BUILD NEW** (custom Zimmermann, nothing to start from) · **REUSE AS-IS** (base SFCC or existing Zimmermann component, no change) · **OVERRIDE** (base SFCC module exists, we shadow it) · **THEME ONLY** (base component is fine, only needs a theme recipe) · **ALREADY BUILT** (exists on this branch already).

Tier assignment rule to apply: an **atom** renders no other project component; a **molecule** renders only atoms; an **organism** renders at least one molecule. An icon passed as a prop does not count. Slotted children do not count.

**Then answer each of the Lead's four questions explicitly, as its own short section:**
- What is to be built from scratch?
- What is to be reused?
- What is for overriding?
- What is custom vs what is out-of-the-box?

**Also include:**
- **A build order** consistent with atom-first — what to build in what sequence, and what blocks what.
- **What the current PR #57 got structurally wrong vs the footer precedent**, concretely. (Known: only one component sits under `ui-kits/`; two of the three new components have no theme recipe; the breadcrumb shadows a shared SFCC component consumed by the PLP.)
- **Token gaps** from the Figma spec that need a designer decision rather than an invented value.
- **Anything in SFCC-89's scope that has no Figma design** — flag it rather than guessing.

## Rules
- Cite `file:line` or `git show <branch>:<path>` for everything.
- Distinguish VERIFIED from inferred. If the footer branch does something you cannot explain, say so.
- Do not invent design values or component APIs.
- Note that `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` has no rules file on `develop` — the layout convention is real but not citable. Say where you got it from.
- Do not propose touching Tier 1 files.

## Output
Write to `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/723a905e-37fe-4505-9a24-e817fe4260ab/scratchpad/q-decomposition.md` (create the directory if needed).

Then give a condensed version in your final report message, leading with the decomposition table.

Four of your five answered now; two agents are working the architectural ones.

## 1. Fonts — you're right, my framing was backwards

I had it as a risk: "#55 carries a `frozenFiles.md` asserting self-hosted fonts, which would contradict the licence position on `develop` — flag it before it lands." If self-hosting is the agreed approach and #55 is the vehicle, then that's not a contradiction to flag, it's the newer position arriving. I'll strike it from §3 and §9.

What survives is narrower and still useful: **on this branch today there are no font binaries**, so every visual check Jhoan did rendered the fallback face. That's not a defect in his work or in #55 — it's a sequencing fact. Once #55 lands, type metrics become measurable and SFCC-732/733 become QA-able. Before then they aren't, by anyone.

## 2. Why it replaces the whole PDP — and yes, you can do what you're describing

The mechanical answer is that **it doesn't change the OOTB page at all.** The base 876-line page is untouched and still in the bundle. What happened is narrower: `overrides/app/routes.tsx` registers `/product/:productId` ahead of the base routes, so our 95-line page wins the URL. The OOTB page is still there, just unreachable.

So why does it *lose* everything? Because the file was written from scratch — 48 lines in the first commit against an 876-line base — rather than copied and then edited. That's the **copy-first rule** in `AGENTS.md`, and it exists for precisely this outcome: copy the base file, convert it, verify it renders identically, *then* insert your component. Skipping that step is the whole story here. The same omission explains the breadcrumb restyling the PLP.

So yes — override, keep everything OOTB, insert only what's built. That's the intended default, not a special accommodation. I've got an agent working out whether the *right seam* is the page or actually `product-view` (which may already render name and price, in which case the page never needs touching), plus the concrete file shape. That's the part worth waiting for.

## 3. The breadcrumb — your instinct is correct, there's no design

**It's in the ticket, not in Figma.** SFCC-89's AC has two Given/When/Thens for it:

> *"a breadcrumb trail is displayed underneath the product pictures reflecting the product's category path (e.g. HOME / NEW / DRESSES / [PRODUCT NAME])"*
> *"when the click is registered, then the shopper is navigated to the corresponding category page"*

And in the measured Figma spec: **zero occurrences.** The ticket's own attachment crop ends above where it would sit.

So every visual decision in that component — the `/` separator, the uppercase, the type size, the spacing, bottom-of-page placement — was invented from a one-line text example. That's a genuine requirements gap, not a build error, and it's worth naming as one: an AC mandated a component with no design behind it.

It also compounds the ownership problem. **SFCC-578 "SEO — Breadcrumb Component (PLP & PDP)"** is Squad B's, still To Do, and SFCC-573 (JSON-LD) and SFCC-570 (heading hierarchy) both depend on it existing. Confluence 04.72 says *"each component is owned by the earliest epic in the sequence where it appears"*, which argues for PDP owning it — but nobody recorded that on either ticket.

My read: this is the strongest candidate to cut from #57 entirely. No design, another squad's ticket, and it's currently changing the PLP.

## 4. E2E — not overengineering, but it did jump a gate

Numbers first:

| | E2E added |
|---|---|
| PR #57 (this one) | 324 lines — `.feature` 65, spec 158, fixtures +74, page object +33 |
| PR #55 (footer) | **zero** |
| `develop` baseline | one homepage smoke feature + spec |

**The `.feature` file is required**, so that part isn't excess — `testing.md`'s checklist says "New user journey → has a `.feature` file", and viewing a product is a journey.

**The spec is the problem, and it's a process skip rather than gold-plating.** The rule is a three-stage workflow, stated flatly:

> *"2. Lead QA validates in plain English — **no Playwright code is written until sign-off**"*
> *"3. Playwright spec is generated only after the `.feature` is approved"*

Both the feature and 158 lines of spec are on the branch. Unless QA signed off the feature first, the spec was written out of order — which risks throwing the work away, the opposite of diligence. Worth asking Jhoan whether that sign-off happened; I can't tell from the repo.

And a chunk of it won't run where it matters anyway: 3 tests are skipped, the file is `.spec.js` with no `.p0.` segment so the SIT gate can never select it, and there's no `e2e_pdp` group in `qa.yml` so every PDP change triggers the full suite. Credit where due — the tags *are* correct (`@pdp`, `@SFCC-89`), and price fixtures cover six regions, so that's better than I said in the report.

**On the footer having none:** defensible. The footer isn't a user journey; its interactive behaviour belongs in Storybook `play`, which is a different layer. I haven't audited #55's `play` coverage this session, so I won't claim it's complete — but "no Playwright on the footer" isn't the gap it looks like.

## 5. The decomposition — in flight

The atoms/molecules/organisms breakdown against the story, Figma, and #55's established pattern is running now. It'll come back with a verdict per element — build new / reuse / override / theme-only / already built — plus a build order.

---

**One ask:** you said some findings are misaligned with what you know. Tell me which and I'll correct them at the source rather than leaving them to propagate — the fonts one had already reached three sections of that report before you caught it.

False alarm — and worth being precise about why, because it looks convincing.

Base `url.js:90` is `(category) => encodeURI(`/category/${category.id}`)` — **one parameter**. The base breadcrumb calls it as `categoryUrlBuilder(category, intl.locale)`, but JavaScript silently discards the extra argument. Our override's inlined copy produces byte-identical output. **No locale prefix is lost, because base never added one** — the `/en-au/` prefix comes from the routing layer, not this builder.

My earlier "ruled out" stands. Now the claim that's actionable if true.

## Condensed report

### Answer to the Lead: yes

PR #57 replaces the whole page not because the override mechanism forces it to, but because `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` was written from scratch (95 lines) instead of ported from the 876-line base, which `AGENTS.md` > Rules > **Copy-first rule** already required. Nearly everything the base page provides is orthogonal to SFCC-89 and can be kept verbatim.

**One genuine exception.** The name+price block lives in a module-private `ProductViewHeader` (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-view/index.jsx:63-99`), rendered **twice** (`:584-591` mobile, `:643-650` desktop), and `ProductView` has **no `children`, no render-prop, no slot** near the name/price — only `imageGalleryFooter` (`:621-626`, below the gallery) and `customButtons` (`:494-504`, below the CTAs). Also `<Heading fontSize="2xl">` (`:81`) is an inline prop, so "just theme it" is unavailable. So `PdpProductInfo` cannot displace it without owning a copy of `product-view`.

### What the current override actually lost
1. **All SEO** — no `<Helmet>` (base `:658-669`), and `useProduct` (override `:25`) drops the nine-entry `expand` list including `page_meta_tags` (base `:115-125`), so `pageTitle`/`pageMetaTags` don't exist on the object. Worst loss on an SEO-critical storefront.
2. **404** — `HTTPNotFound`/`HTTPError` (base `:191-210`) gone; a bad SKU returns HTTP 200.
3. **`Cache-Control`** `s-maxage=900, stale-while-revalidate=900` (base `:85-90`).
4. **Pricing fidelity** — `perPricebook: true` (base `:114`) gone; hand-rolled `intl.formatNumber` instead of `DisplayPrice`.
5. Gallery, swatches, quantity, add-to-bag, `InformationAccordion`, all three `RecommendedProducts` rails, Einstein/Data Cloud/Active Data beacons.
6. `layerStyle="page"` (base `:649`) — page gutters/max-width/centering.

`<Island>` is **inert** here (`config/default.js:40 partialHydrationEnabled: false`; `island/index.jsx:88-91` early-returns children), so that one costs nothing.

### Recommendation (not hedged)
Port the page copy-first, **plus** a scoped fork of `product-view` adding **one optional `renderHeader` prop** defaulting to the existing private header. Rejected overriding `product-view` alone: the page-level capabilities aren't in it, and its blast radius is four surfaces — PDP, cart (`pages/cart/index.jsx:34,35,58`), wishlist (`wishlist-primary-action.jsx:11`), bonus-product flow — via `product-view-modal` / `bonus-product-view-modal`. An optional default-preserving prop contains that by construction and matches `overrideStyling.md:133-146`'s bridge pattern. Fallback if the 1054-line fork can't be scoped this sprint: port the page only, skip `ProductView` — recovers six of seven losses. **This is a scope decision for the Lead**, not mine to take.

### Two findings worth escalating beyond the question
- **`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:95-103` is factually wrong.** `pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js:128-146` returns false when the issuer is inside `overrides/` (`:144`), and its own doc comment (`:116-127`) states it verbatim; `config.js:165` then aliases straight to `node_modules`. So a base-path import from `overrides/` gets the **base** file **in the production build too** — not just Storybook/Vitest. The advice (use relative paths) is right; the rationale understates the risk.
- **The `breadcrumb` override is already leaking into base consumers.** `product-view/index.jsx:45,75` and `product-list/partials/page-header.jsx:14,20` are base-template files, so they get our breadcrumb in the app build. Ours (`overrides/app/components/breadcrumb/index.tsx:47`) drops the `{...rest}` passthrough, always prepends HOME, swaps the chevron for `/`, and drops `data-testid="sf-crumb-item"` — the PLP header silently changed and lost a test selector. Live bug independent of this decision.

Also flagged: `.claude/rules/overrides.md` doesn't exist despite three references from `overrideStyling.md` (`:4`, `:91`, `:139`), and that file cites six other precedent paths (`theme/components/imageGallery.ts`, `swatchGroup.ts`, `components/product-tile/`, `link/`, `swatch-group/`, `productDetailOptions/`) that don't exist on this branch. Creating `overrides/app/components/product-view/` would land in a path that is in **no** tier list, though it is functionally Tier 2.</result>

Both confirmed. Here's everything.

## 2. Composition — yes, with one genuine exception

**The general answer is yes**, and copy-first is the mechanism that makes it the default. Port the base page, convert to TypeScript, verify it renders identically, then insert your components. Everything OOTB stays OOTB.

**The exception is name and price specifically.** They're rendered by a module-private `ProductViewHeader` inside `product-view/index.jsx:63-99`, called **twice** (mobile `:584`, desktop `:643`). `ProductView` exposes only two slots — `imageGalleryFooter` (below the gallery) and `customButtons` (below the CTAs) — neither anywhere near the header. And `<Heading fontSize="2xl">` at `:81` is an inline prop, so a theme recipe can't reach it either.

So for the four other fields — description, style code, model copy, breadcrumb — a straight page port works. For name and price you need to touch `product-view`.

**Recommended:** port the page copy-first, plus a narrowly scoped fork of `product-view` adding **one optional `renderHeader` prop that defaults to the existing private header**. Default-preserving, so the other three consumers are untouched by construction. Overriding `product-view` outright was considered and rejected — its blast radius is four surfaces: PDP, cart (`pages/cart/index.jsx:34,35,58`), wishlist, and the bonus-product flow.

**Cheaper fallback if the fork won't scope this sprint:** port the page only and leave `ProductView` alone. That recovers six of the seven losses and defers just the name/price placement.

**What the port gets back, concretely:** `<Helmet>` SEO plus the nine-entry `expand` list including `page_meta_tags` · `HTTPNotFound`/`HTTPError` so a bad SKU stops returning HTTP 200 · `Cache-Control: s-maxage=900` · `perPricebook: true` for price fidelity · the accordions, all three recommendation rails, and the Einstein/Data Cloud beacons · `layerStyle="page"` for gutters and max-width.

**One item off that list** — I told you `<Island>` hydration was lost. It's inert: `config/default.js:40` sets `partialHydrationEnabled: false` and `island/index.jsx:88` early-returns children. Absent, but costs nothing.

## 5. Decomposition

| Element | Tier | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Product name | atom | **BUILD NEW** — extract; `textStyle="heading3"` matches SFCC-732 exactly |
| Price | atom | **BUILD NEW** — extract |
| Description | atom | **BUILD NEW** — the sanitiser boundary deserves one auditable atom |
| Model copy + style code | atom | **BUILD NEW** — one atom with a tone variant; both map to `caption` |
| Static info block | molecule | **ALREADY BUILT, wrong tier** — renders zero project components, so by your own rule it's an atom doing five atoms' work |
| Crumb link | atom | **REUSE** — `ZimmNavItem` from #55 already does the a/button switch, `aria-current`, `isSafeHref`, hover underline. Needs a `breadcrumb` variant, ~10 lines. Blocked on #55 merging. |
| Separator | — | keep internal, no story needed |
| Breadcrumb trail | molecule | **BUILD NEW as Zimmermann** — and move it out of `components/breadcrumb/` |
| Toolbar bar | atom | **ALREADY BUILT** — the only component in the right directory |
| PDP hero grid | organism | **NOT THIS TICKET** — SFCC-723 owns it; currently inline in the page |
| Gallery, swatches, size, CTA, accordions, badges, wishlist | organism | **STAYS OOTB** — zero overrides exist, all Squad B |

**From scratch:** four atoms, one molecule, two theme recipes. Notably **four of the five atoms need no recipe at all** — their entire spec is one registered `textStyle` plus one colour token, same call #55 made for `zimmIcon` and `zimmLogo`.

**Reused:** `ZimmPageToolbar` (its other two variants are already built and unused), base `Skeleton`/`Box`/`Text`, the SDK hooks, `extractModelLine`, and the `ProductPage` test-ids — preserve those or ten E2E tests break. Biggest win is `ZimmNavItem`; don't fork it into this branch.

**For overriding:** only `pages/product-detail`. Nothing else — including the one thing currently built as an override.

**Custom vs OOTB:** everything visible here is custom. Base SFCC has no product-name, style-code or model-fit component at all.

**No Figma for the breadcrumb**, as you suspected. The only candidate is an instance called "PLP Bar desktop" at 1440×53 — and if that's it, the current 32px vertical padding (64px total) doesn't fit in 53px.

## Two places the audit was wrong and Jhoan was right

**The theme file's escape hatches are justified.** An agent claimed `PRICE_TEXT` is byte-identical to `textStyles.price`, so the "pending sign-off" comment was stale and three `var()` escapes were deletable. Not so — `PRICE_TEXT` resolves `--zimm-font-family-body` to **FONT_REGULAR**, while `textStyles.price` uses **FONT_MEDIUM**. Adopting the textStyle would change the font family. That is precisely what his comment names: *"unresolved (FONT_REGULAR vs FONT_MEDIUM) pending UI-designer sign-off."* The letter-spacing difference is nil — `letterSpacings.sm` is `'0'`. **His caution was correct; add it to the designer batch instead of "fixing" it.**

**The breadcrumb locale claim was a false alarm**, as covered above — base ignores the locale argument it appears to pass.

## A rules file that's wrong in a way that raises the stakes

`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:95-103` says a base-path import from inside an override "will build and run correctly in the shipped app" and only misbehaves in Storybook and Vitest. **That's wrong.** The resolver's own comment explains why:

> *"this is very important, to avoid circular imports, check that the `issuer` (requesting context) isn't the overrides directory"*

When the importing file lives in `overrides/`, the redirect never fires — so you get the base component **in production too**, not just in the test harnesses. The advice (use relative paths) is right; the stated reason badly understates the risk. Worth correcting, since it's the file people consult before wiring up exactly this.

## One ruling I need from you

`ZimmButton` is filed as an **atom** but renders `ZimmIcon` — which under the rule you're using makes it a **molecule**. That's not pedantry: it decides where the crumb link and the meta atom land. Which way do you want it — strict (renders any project component ⇒ molecule), or does an icon not count?

content.text:
Good — that changes the answer meaningfully. Here's what #55 actually hands you:

**Atoms:** `zimmButton`, `zimmIcon`, `zimmLogo`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmTextInput` · **Molecule:** `zimmInputAction` · **Recipes:** `zimmNavItem.ts`, `zimmTextInput.ts`, plus `navConstants.ts` and `recipeGuards.test.ts` · **Fonts:** both Futura Round faces and `fontFace.tsx`.

Note that only **two of five atoms have a recipe**. `zimmIcon` and `zimmLogo` have none — their spec is a textStyle plus a token, so there was nothing for a recipe to hold. That's the precedent, and it applies directly here: most of what SFCC-89 needs is exactly that shape.

---

## Phase 0 — land the decisions first, before any code

Six things change the shape of the build, so they're cheaper to answer now than to rework later:

1. **Breadcrumb: in or out.** No Figma design exists, and SFCC-578 is Squad B's. My recommendation is out — it's the cleanest cut available and it removes a cross-squad conflict, a PLP regression, and an undesigned component in one move.
2. **`modelFit` vs `c_sizeFit`.** SFCC-26 created `modelFit` for this exact line. If it isn't in the sandbox yet, the interim scrape needs an owner and a removal ticket, not a silent workaround.
3. **Style code source** — master style number, not `product.id`.
4. **Sanitiser approach** — determines what the description atom looks like, so it's a prerequisite, not a follow-up.
5. **Composition depth** — page port alone, or page port plus the `product-view` `renderHeader` fork. Page-only defers just name/price placement and is a much smaller diff.
6. **The `ZimmButton` tier ruling** — atom or molecule. It decides where the new atoms land.

Plus the designer batch, which now includes a question #57 surfaced correctly: **FONT_REGULAR or FONT_MEDIUM for price and meta copy.** With #55's fonts merged, that becomes answerable by looking at it — which it isn't today.

## Phase 1 — copy-first, and stop

Copy base `pages/product-detail/index.jsx` to `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`, convert to TypeScript, add the temporary marker log, and **verify the full PDP still works** — add-to-bag, swatches, quantity, gallery, accordions, recommendations, SEO tags in the SSR HTML, bad SKU returning 404.

Then pause and let someone test it before a single functional change.

This one step is the difference between the two PRs. Everything after it is purely additive, so there's no mechanism by which capability gets lost. #57's entire integration-layer problem traces to skipping it.

## Phase 2 — atoms, each tiny

Four atoms under `ui-kits/atoms/`, following the `zimmIcon`/`zimmLogo` shape — component plus story, **no recipe** unless it genuinely needs variants or interaction state:

| Atom | Spec |
|---|---|
| `zimmProductName` | `textStyle="heading3"` — an exact match to what SFCC-732 asserts |
| `zimmProductPrice` | `textStyle="price"`, pending the font-weight ruling |
| `zimmProductProse` | the sanitised-HTML boundary — one auditable place, since semgrep enforces it |
| `zimmProductMeta` | `caption`, with a tone variant covering both model copy and style code |

The payoff is the reason to bother: SFCC-91, SFCC-92 and SFCC-194 all need a name, a price and prose. Right now they can import nothing, which is why SFCC-91 is already repeating the structural mistake on its own branch.

## Phase 3 — the molecule

`zimmProductInfo` composes those four atoms and nothing else. That's a real molecule under your rule, unlike the current block which renders zero project components.

If the breadcrumb stays in scope, it goes at `ui-kits/molecules/zimmBreadcrumb/` — **not** `components/breadcrumb/`, which is the path that shadows the shared SFCC module the PLP renders. Each crumb reuses `ZimmNavItem`, which already handles the anchor/button switch, `aria-current`, safe-href checking and the hover underline. Don't fork it.

## Phase 4 — insert, then clean up

Drop the molecule into the ported page (or through `renderHeader` if you took the fork), remove the copy-first markers, and name every base behaviour you deliberately changed in the PR body.

## Phase 5 — verification that proves something

The mechanical checks are cheap and none of them are CI-gated, so they're honour-system: `tsc --noEmit`, `lint`, `vitest`, `test-storybook` (a11y genuinely gates at `error`).

The one that actually matters is a named parity checklist against the pre-change PDP — add-to-bag, swatch selection, quantity, gallery, accordions, recommendation rails, SEO tags present in the served HTML, bad SKU → 404. A green build tells you nothing about any of those.

Then gherkin-first, in order: draft the `.feature`, get Lead QA sign-off, **then** generate the spec. #57 wrote 158 lines of spec before that gate, which is why some of it may be throwaway.

## What stays OOTB, explicitly

Gallery, swatches, size selector, add-to-bag, accordions, badges, wishlist, recommendations. Zero overrides exist for any of them, all are Squad B's, and each has its own ticket. Under this approach they keep working untouched the whole time.

---

**One caveat that sits above all of it:** the SEO restoration is theoretical until Integration resolves the server-rendering finding. If no page server-renders, `<Helmet>` tags never reach a crawler. Worth knowing so nobody counts SEO as delivered on the strength of the code being present.

Want me to write this up as a build plan document alongside the takeover report? And I still need the `ZimmButton` ruling — it's the one thing here I can't decide for you.

content.text:
That settles it, and it reverses the report's headline finding. Correct URLs:

| URL | Result |
|---|---|
| `/` | **200**, 264 KB — renders fine |
| `/search?q=dress` | **200**, 338 KB — fine |
| `/login` | **200**, 280 KB — fine |
| `/category/womens` | **404**, 228 KB — a *proper* 404 |
| `/product/8637DS241-3` | **502** `{"message": "Internal server error"}` |
| `/product/NOT-A-REAL-SKU` | **502** — same, SKU-independent |

## Where the finding came from, and why it was wrong

The original probe used URLs like `/en-au/product/8637DS241-3`. That prefix looks right but isn't this project's scheme — `config/default.js` sets `site: 'path'`, `locale: 'path'`, `showDefaults: false`, and **ZimmermannAU's locale is `en`, not `en-AU`**. Since AU/en is the default and defaults are hidden, the real URL is just `/product/...` with no prefix.

So every `/en-au/*` probe hit a path that matches nothing — and got swallowed by the `/:slug` Contentful catch-all in `overrides/app/routes.tsx`, which is registered without `exact: true`. That page renders `<Box p={8} display="flex" justifyContent="center"><Spinner size="xl" /></Box>`, which is byte-for-byte the markup I found in `<main>`.

Seeing that same spinner on six consecutive routes looked like overwhelming confirmation of a storefront-wide SSR failure. It was six repetitions of the same wrong URL.

## What's actually true

**Retracted:** "no page server-renders anywhere." Homepage, search and login all server-render properly, and the category route returns a real 404 — which incidentally proves the base page's `HTTPNotFound` handling works, the very thing the PDP override dropped.

**Confirmed and now reproduced live:** the PDP hard-502s on valid and invalid SKUs alike. That's the `__WEBPACK_DEFAULT_EXPORT__` TDZ from the CI log — `isomorphic-dompurify` running `new JSDOM()` at module-evaluation time. **It is this PR's defect, not a pre-existing platform one.**

**And the reviewers are back on the hook.** I told you the "nobody opened the preview" criticism didn't hold because they'd have seen a spinner either way. Wrong — anyone who opened the preview and clicked a product would have hit a hard 502 in one click. That criticism stands after all.

One genuine minor find survives: the `/:slug` catch-all lacking `exact: true` means any mistyped URL renders a Contentful spinner instead of a 404. Pre-existing, low severity, worth a ticket.

Let me correct the report — it currently has this as the #1 ranked item and builds a fairness argument on it.

## 2. The bigger problem I found by accident

**No page on this storefront is server-rendered. On any route. On any environment I could reach.**

I went looking for the reported PDP crash on the preview environment and found something else: every
URL returns HTTP 200 with the app shell rendered and a **loading spinner** where the page content
should be.

| URL | Result |
|---|---|
| preview `/` | 200, spinner |
| preview `/en-au/product/8637DS241-3` | 200, spinner |
| preview `/en-au/product/DEFINITELY-NOT-A-SKU` | 200, spinner |
| preview `/en-au/category/womens` | 200, spinner |
| preview `/en-au/search?q=dress` | 200, spinner |
| preview `/en-au/login` | 200, spinner |
| **`test` tier `/`** | 200, spinner |
| **`test` tier `/en-au/category/womens`** | 200, spinner |

Supporting detail: the PDP's HTML is identical to the homepage's apart from the canonical URL. Its
`<title>` is `Retail React App` — the fallback, not a product name. The strings `Style Code` and
`Unable to load product information` appear **zero** times in the served HTML. Same output for curl,
for a real Chrome user-agent, and for Googlebot. The shell itself *is* server-rendered — header,
footer, the SVG sprite, the full theme. It's the page components that never arrive.

And the preview genuinely is running this PR's code — the served chunk matches my local build byte
for byte.

**What this costs.** The project brief opens with *"Must be robust and secure and SEO-friendly"* and
sets a ≤2s p75 mobile LCP budget. Client-rendered spinners defeat both. Every "compare the preview
against Figma" review anyone has ever done on this project has been reviewing a client-rendered page.

**My best guess at the cause, stated as a guess.** Every page in base Salesforce's route table is
wrapped in `loadable(() => import(...), {fallback})`. A correct shell plus a spinner in `<main>` is
exactly what you get when the server-side chunk resolution doesn't happen and the `fallback` renders
instead. That points at `ChunkExtractor` / `loadable-stats.json` wiring in `overrides/app/ssr.js`
and `overrides/app/ssr/` — **Tier 1, Integration-owned, and one of the four absolutely-untouchable
files.** Do not go near it. Report it.

**Two things this changes immediately.**

First, it clears the reviewers. The criticism that nobody opened the preview URL doesn't survive:
opening it shows a spinner on the PDP *and* on the homepage, indistinguishable. Any reviewer who
looked would reasonably conclude "previews don't SSR here" and move on. Don't use that as a stick.

Second, the reported PDP crash and this finding are consistent, not contradictory. The crash happens
where SSR actually evaluates the page module — which is where the CI Playwright run served from. On
MRT it's **masked**, because MRT never evaluates the page module server-side at all. Which also
means: **the MRT preview is not a usable SSR smoke test on this project.** Any process fix that says
"hit the preview and check the status code" would have produced a false pass here.

| URL | Result |

`isomorphic-dompurify` executes `new JSDOM()` at module-evaluation time, and
`pdpProductInfo/index.tsx:2` imports it at module scope, so the page module cannot be evaluated
server-side at all.

**This is this PR's defect.** Not a platform problem, not pre-existing, and not Integration's to fix.
Removing the module-scope import removes the 502.

Note also what the category route proves: base's 404 handling genuinely works. That is one of the
capabilities the page override drops (§1), so a bad SKU on the current code would return HTTP 200
once the 502 is fixed — a second, separate defect hiding behind the first.

**ZimmermannAU's locale is `en`, not `en-AU`**. Since AU/en is the default and defaults are hidden,

`overrides/app/routes.tsx`, which is registered **without `exact: true`** and so swallows any

`<Box p={8} display="flex" justifyContent="center"><Spinner size="xl" /></Box>` — byte-for-byte the

Report corrected — 714 lines, no surviving trace of the retracted claim.

## Answering your question directly

**Where it came from:** a probe of `/en-au/product/...` and five sibling URLs on the PR preview. All six returned HTTP 200 with a Chakra spinner in `<main>`, so the conclusion drawn was "nothing server-renders anywhere — pre-existing platform defect."

**Why it was wrong:** `/en-au/` isn't a URL on this storefront. `config/default.js` sets `site: 'path'`, `locale: 'path'`, `showDefaults: false`, and ZimmermannAU's locale is **`en`**, not `en-AU`. Default site and locale are hidden, so the real PDP URL is bare — `/product/8637DS241-3`.

Every `/en-au/*` request therefore matched no route and fell into the `/:slug` Contentful catch-all, which is registered **without `exact: true`** and swallows any unmatched multi-segment path. That page renders `<Box p={8} display="flex" justifyContent="center"><Spinner size="xl" /></Box>` — I traced the served CSS back to `pages/experience/index.tsx:36-37` byte-for-byte.

Six identical spinners felt like strong confirmation. It was one wrong URL, repeated six times.

**What's actually true:** homepage 200, search 200, login 200, category a proper 404 — and `/product/*` returns a hard **502 on every SKU**. That's the JSDOM-at-import crash, now reproduced on the live preview rather than inferred from a CI artifact.

## What that changes

Three things flipped, and two of them matter to how you handle people:

- **The 502 is this PR's defect**, not a platform problem. Nothing to escalate to Integration as an SSR investigation — just the dependency, as a defect report.
- **The reviewers are back on the hook.** I told you they were excused because the preview would have shown them nothing. Wrong: one click on any product would have surfaced a 502 on 18 Aug. That excuse is withdrawn in the report.
- **The "preview isn't a usable SSR smoke test" guidance was backwards.** It *is* usable. What was missing is reading the URL scheme out of `config/` before constructing a test URL — which I've written into the doc-corrections section in place of the wrong advice.

One small real finding survives: that `/:slug` catch-all without `exact: true` means any mistyped URL renders a Contentful spinner instead of a 404. Bad for SEO and for debugging. Worth its own ticket.

**The broader lesson I'd take from this:** a probe that returns the same answer six times can be six confirmations or one repeated mistake, and those look identical from the outside. The tell I missed was that the spinner didn't match either route fallback in the codebase — both are `Skeleton`, not `Spinner`. Chasing which component actually emitted the markup is what unravelled it, and that check was available from the start.
