questions.question: PR #55 hasn't merged yet (still blocked on human code-owner approval). Where should the new branch be cut from?

options.label: From develop now, rebase when #55 lands (Recommended)
options.description: Keeps momentum on an already-overdue story. The four product-info atoms we need (name, price, prose, meta) don't overlap with #55's five (button, icon, logo, navItem, textInput), so rebase conflict risk is genuinely low. Cost: no fonts until the rebase, so no type-metric validation, and no ZimmNavItem for the crumb link.

options.label: Wait for #55 to merge, then cut
options.description: Cleanest possible base — fonts available so visual checks are real, ZimmNavItem available for reuse, no rebase at all. Cost: blocked entirely until #55 clears review, and you know that timeline better than I do.

options.label: Cut from #55's branch directly
options.description: Everything available immediately without waiting. Cost: builds on unmerged history, so if #55 changes during review we inherit the churn, and the eventual PR diff is muddled against develop.

questions.question: How much of PR #57's work should this build reuse?

options.label: Component + recipe only, rebuild the rest (Recommended)
options.description: PdpProductInfo and its ZimmPdpProductInfo recipe are independently the best example of the house pattern in the repo — the recipe's escape hatches and its FONT_REGULAR/FONT_MEDIUM note are genuinely good work. Split the component into atoms, keep the recipe's substance. Discard the page, breadcrumb and route change.

options.label: Nothing — true clean build
options.description: Maximum clarity, no inherited assumptions, and the plan writes itself. Cost: throws away the one part of #57 that's genuinely exemplary, and re-derives design decisions already made correctly.

options.label: Cherry-pick broadly
options.description: Take the component, recipe, extractModelLine util, the ProductWithSizeFit type, and the .feature file. Fastest path to parity. Cost: also inherits the c_sizeFit assumption and the E2E fixture shape, both of which have open questions.

questions.question: Base renders product name and price inside a module-private header in product-view, with an inline fontSize prop that a theme recipe can't reach. There is no slot near it. How do we handle ACs 1 and 2?

options.label: Page port + a scoped product-view fork adding one optional renderHeader prop
options.description: Delivers all six ACs with correct Zimmermann styling. The prop defaults to the existing private header, so cart, wishlist and the bonus-product flow are untouched by construction. Cost: forking a 1054-line file, and it lands in a path that no tier list currently covers.

options.label: Page port only — accept base's name/price styling for now
options.description: Delivers description, style code, model copy and layout cleanly with a much smaller diff. Name and price still render, just with base SFCC typography rather than the Figma spec. Cost: ACs 1 and 2 are functionally met but visually wrong, and SFCC-732 will fail at QA.

options.label: Page port only, and re-scope ACs 1 and 2 out
options.description: Honest smallest-slice: deliver what can be delivered well, and raise name/price styling as its own ticket against product-view. Cost: needs Jas to agree to re-scope, and the story loses its two headline criteria.

questions.question: The breadcrumb has no Figma design, and SFCC-578 (Squad B) owns it as a shared PLP+PDP component. Is it in this build?

options.label: Out — hand it to SFCC-578 (Recommended)
options.description: Removes an undesigned component, a cross-squad conflict, and the PLP regression in one cut. SFCC-573 (JSON-LD) and SFCC-570 (heading hierarchy) already depend on SFCC-578 existing, so Squad B has to build it regardless. Cost: SFCC-89's AC-6 goes unmet and needs re-scoping with Jas.

options.label: In, built properly as a Zimmermann molecule
options.description: Meets AC-6, and done right this time: lives under ui-kits/molecules/, reuses ZimmNavItem, never shadows the shared SFCC module, so the PLP is untouched. Cost: still no design to build against, and you'd be delivering Squad B's component without their agreement.

options.label: In, but blocked until a design exists
options.description: Keeps it in scope and forces the design gap to be resolved rather than invented. Cost: adds a hard dependency on the designer to a story that's already five days overdue.

# 7. `ZimmNavItem` full API (`.../atoms/zimmNavItem/index.tsx`, 62 lines)

`type ZimmNavItemProps` at `:9-26` (not exported):

| Prop | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | required | Rendered inside the inner `<span>` |
| `href` | `string` | `undefined` | Gates anchor vs button; must also pass `isSafeHref` |
| `active` | `boolean` | `false` | → `aria-current={active ? 'page' : undefined}` on both branches |
| `inverse` | `boolean` | `false` | → recipe variant `'inverse'`, else `'light'` (`:32`) |
| `onClick` | `(e: React.MouseEvent<HTMLAnchorElement \| HTMLButtonElement>) => void` | `undefined` | Same handler wired to both branches |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` | `undefined` | Raw inline style |
| `sx` | `SystemStyleObject` | `undefined` | Documented `:24` as "Preferred over `style` — token keys resolve" |

Render branches:
- **Anchor** (`:35-48`) — when `href && isSafeHref(href)`: `<chakra.a href aria-current onClick __css={styles} sx style><span>{label}</span></chakra.a>`
- **Button** (`:50-60`) — otherwise: `<chakra.button type="button" aria-current onClick __css={styles} sx style><span>{label}</span></chakra.button>`

Both branches: identical `aria-current` handling, identical `__css`/`sx`/`style` plumbing, label always wrapped in a bare `<span>` (the underline carrier targeted by `'& > span'` in the recipe). Header comment `:5-7` records why protocol-relative `//` is excluded from the allowlist.

`isSafeHref` (`overrides/app/utils/safeHref.ts:36`): `/^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i`, applied **after** WHATWG-style normalisation (`:34`) that strips leading/trailing C0-or-space and removes tab/LF/CR anywhere.

**Not present:** no `as` prop, no `target`/`rel`, no `ref`, no `children`, no `size`, no `id`/`data-*`/`aria-label` passthrough, no React Router `Link` integration (it emits a plain `<a href>`; the footer's logo instead uses `<chakra.button>` + a `history.push` handler — `footer/index.tsx:519-525`).

## Could it serve as a breadcrumb crumb link?

**In its favour (VERIFIED):** safe-href gating is exactly what a CMS/route-derived crumb needs; `aria-current="page"` is already supported; hover-underline is the standard crumb affordance; `sx` is the sanctioned per-consumer override and there is already a working precedent for reshaping it from outside — the footer passes `sx={styles.legalLink}` (`footer/index.tsx:393`) where `footer.ts:396-404` supplies `textStyle: 'footer'`, `color: var(--zimm-color-text-muted)`, `paddingY: 'xs'`, `paddingX: 0`, with a comment noting no height override is needed because the baseStyle uses `minHeight`.

**Blockers (VERIFIED):**
1. **The variant is derived, not a prop.** `const variant = inverse ? 'inverse' : 'light';` (`:32`). A third recipe variant is *unreachable from outside*. Adding `breadcrumb` also has to compose with `inverse` (a 4-way matrix), which a single boolean cannot express.
2. **Typography is nav typography, hard-coded in baseStyle.** `textStyle: 'navigation'` (`zimmNavItem.ts:17`) = `FONT_MEDIUM`, `fontSizes['3xs']` (12px), weight medium, `letterSpacings.sm`, **`textTransform: 'uppercase'`** (`foundation/typography.ts:211-218`) — plus a `fontFamily: 'var(--zimm-font-family-body)'` on the very next line (`:18`) that deliberately overrides the textStyle's family.
3. **The current crumb has no correct rendering.** Omitting `href` gives you a `<button>` (`:50-60`), which is wrong semantics for a non-interactive current page. There is no "render as plain text/`<span>`" path.
4. **No separator, no list wrapper, no `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">`/`<ol>`** — those belong to a parent, not this atom.
5. Geometry is nav-row geometry: `minHeight: var(--zimm-scale-xl)` (24px), `paddingBlock: 4.5px`, `justifyContent`/`alignItems: center`.
6. There is a base SFCC `Breadcrumb` at `app/components/breadcrumb/index.jsx` with **no** Zimmermann override yet (`.claude/registry/components.md:15`), `Layout/` is the documented story category for it (`components.md:119`), and a recipe named `Breadcrumb` would **fail** `recipeGuards.test.ts:212`. It must be `ZimmBreadcrumb`.

**What a `breadcrumb` variant would need to add (INFERRED from the above — not read anywhere):**
- A real `variant?: 'nav' | 'breadcrumb'` prop, composed with `inverse` using the same string-concat pattern zimmButton already uses (`zimmButton/index.tsx:60`, `` `${variant}${inverse ? 'Inverse' : ''}` ``) → recipe variants `nav`/`navInverse`/`breadcrumb`/`breadcrumbInverse`, or a `defaultProps.variant` shuffle.
- In `zimmNavItem.ts`: a `textStyle` (or explicit fontSize/letterSpacing/`textTransform: 'none'`) override, a `minHeight`/`paddingBlock` reset, and an explicit decision on whether the `'& > span'` hover underline survives — note that removing it from a variant requires `_hover: { '& > span': { borderBottomColor: 'transparent' } }`, since the base rule sets `currentColor`.
- A `current`/`isCurrentPage` concept producing `<span aria-current="page">` rather than the button fallback.
- A separate `ZimmBreadcrumb` molecule for the `<nav>`/`<ol>`/separator, story-titled `Layout/ZimmBreadcrumb`.

# 8. Deliberate deviations from the repo's written rules — do not "fix" these

All of (a)–(f), (h), (i), (k), (l) are intentional and, except where noted, documented in-file.

**(a) Folder location is undocumented.** `.claude/rules/conventions.md:81-94` says "each component lives in its own folder under `overrides/app/components/`" and shows a **flat** `productTile/` example; `.claude/skills/new-component/SKILL.md:29` says `overrides/app/components/<componentName>/index.tsx`. The atoms live at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/<name>/`. I grepped `ui-kits` across `.claude`, `.docs`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github` — the **only** hits are the six auto-generated registry rows (`.claude/registry/components.md:83-88`). The atomic-design nesting is a convention this branch established, not a written rule.

**(b) No default export.** `new-component/SKILL.md:30` says "named export (`export function <ComponentName>`) plus default export". Every atom is `export const X = (…) => {}` with **no** default export and no `function` keyword. This satisfies `components.md:13` ("No default exports of anonymous functions") and contradicts the skill. Follow the code.

Noted on all four — and "reference it so we don't build blindly" is the right distinction. I'll treat #57 as a reference implementation to read, not a source to copy from.

Standing by on the Figma node for the breadcrumb. Four more that shape the plan:

questions.question: On #55, ZimmButton is filed as an atom but renders ZimmIcon — which under a strict reading makes it a molecule. I need the rule to place the new components consistently.

options.label: Icons don't count toward tier (Recommended)
options.description: An atom may render icons and still be an atom. ZimmButton stays where it is, and our meta atom can render an icon later without being reclassified. Matches what #55 already shipped, so nothing has to move. Cost: the rule needs writing down or it stays tribal.

options.label: Strict — renders any project component means molecule
options.description: Cleanest, most predictable rule, and easiest to check mechanically. Cost: ZimmButton is already merged as an atom, so this reclassifies and moves it — touching #55's work after the fact.

options.label: Tier by semantic concern, not composition
options.description: An atom is one indivisible UI concern regardless of what it renders internally. Most robust as things grow. Cost: the least mechanically checkable of the three, so it relies on judgement in review.

questions.question: SFCC-26 created a `modelFit` attribute specifically for the PDP model line, but it's only 'ready to deploy to UAT' — it may not exist in the sandbox yet. What's our data contract?

options.label: Build against modelFit, guard for absence (Recommended)
options.description: Codes the correct contract per SFCC-26 and renders nothing when the field is missing — which the AC already requires as its negative case. Works today in the sandbox (renders nothing) and starts working automatically once the attribute lands. No rework, no removal ticket.

options.label: Read modelFit, fall back to scraping c_sizeFit
options.description: Shows the copy immediately in every environment. Cost: keeps the English-only regex that fails on 10 of 11 locales, needs an owner and a removal ticket, and the fallback tends to become permanent.

options.label: Descope model copy until SFCC-26 is live
options.description: Cleanest scope boundary — nothing built against an unavailable field. Cost: drops one of the six ACs and needs Jas to agree.

questions.question: The description and model copy are PIM HTML, so they need sanitising before rendering. #57 added isomorphic-dompurify, which is unapproved and crashes SSR. What's our approach?

options.label: Small allow-list sanitiser in overrides/app/utils (Recommended)
options.description: No new dependency, so no Hard Rule #7 gate and no Tier 1 package.json edit. Runs identically on server and client, so the copy stays in the SSR HTML for SEO. Satisfies the semgrep dangerouslySetInnerHTML rule. Cost: we own it, and it needs real unit tests including hostile input.

options.label: isomorphic-dompurify, client-side only
options.description: Battle-tested sanitiser, and the package ships a jsdom-free browser entry so the SSR crash is avoidable. Cost: still needs Integration approval, and the copy is absent from server-rendered HTML — an SEO cost on the fields most worth indexing.

options.label: Render as plain text, no HTML
options.description: Zero risk, zero dependency, trivially testable. Cost: any markup the PIM sends shows as escaped text or gets stripped, so it depends on the fields actually being plain in practice — which nobody has confirmed.

questions.question: What happens to PR #57 while we build this?

options.label: Leave open, close as superseded once ours delivers (Recommended)
options.description: Doesn't discard someone's work before a replacement exists, and keeps the 22 CodeRabbit threads readable as reference. Cost: two open PRs against the same story for a while, so both need a comment explaining which is live.

options.label: Close now with an explanation
options.description: Removes ambiguity immediately and stops anyone reviewing or building on it — SFCC-91 already branched off it. Cost: closing a colleague's PR before the alternative exists, which needs a careful conversation first.

options.label: Convert it to draft
options.description: Signals 'not for review' without closing, and preserves everything. Cost: leaves the story's status genuinely ambiguous in Jira and on the board.

# 7. `ZimmNavItem` full API (`.../atoms/zimmNavItem/index.tsx`, 62 lines)

`type ZimmNavItemProps` at `:9-26` (not exported):

| Prop | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | required | Rendered inside the inner `<span>` |
| `href` | `string` | `undefined` | Gates anchor vs button; must also pass `isSafeHref` |
| `active` | `boolean` | `false` | → `aria-current={active ? 'page' : undefined}` on both branches |
| `inverse` | `boolean` | `false` | → recipe variant `'inverse'`, else `'light'` (`:32`) |
| `onClick` | `(e: React.MouseEvent<HTMLAnchorElement \| HTMLButtonElement>) => void` | `undefined` | Same handler wired to both branches |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` | `undefined` | Raw inline style |
| `sx` | `SystemStyleObject` | `undefined` | Documented `:24` as "Preferred over `style` — token keys resolve" |

Render branches:
- **Anchor** (`:35-48`) — when `href && isSafeHref(href)`: `<chakra.a href aria-current onClick __css={styles} sx style><span>{label}</span></chakra.a>`
- **Button** (`:50-60`) — otherwise: `<chakra.button type="button" aria-current onClick __css={styles} sx style><span>{label}</span></chakra.button>`

Both branches: identical `aria-current` handling, identical `__css`/`sx`/`style` plumbing, label always wrapped in a bare `<span>` (the underline carrier targeted by `'& > span'` in the recipe). Header comment `:5-7` records why protocol-relative `//` is excluded from the allowlist.

`isSafeHref` (`overrides/app/utils/safeHref.ts:36`): `/^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i`, applied **after** WHATWG-style normalisation (`:34`) that strips leading/trailing C0-or-space and removes tab/LF/CR anywhere.

**Not present:** no `as` prop, no `target`/`rel`, no `ref`, no `children`, no `size`, no `id`/`data-*`/`aria-label` passthrough, no React Router `Link` integration (it emits a plain `<a href>`; the footer's logo instead uses `<chakra.button>` + a `history.push` handler — `footer/index.tsx:519-525`).

## Could it serve as a breadcrumb crumb link?

**In its favour (VERIFIED):** safe-href gating is exactly what a CMS/route-derived crumb needs; `aria-current="page"` is already supported; hover-underline is the standard crumb affordance; `sx` is the sanctioned per-consumer override and there is already a working precedent for reshaping it from outside — the footer passes `sx={styles.legalLink}` (`footer/index.tsx:393`) where `footer.ts:396-404` supplies `textStyle: 'footer'`, `color: var(--zimm-color-text-muted)`, `paddingY: 'xs'`, `paddingX: 0`, with a comment noting no height override is needed because the baseStyle uses `minHeight`.

**Blockers (VERIFIED):**
1. **The variant is derived, not a prop.** `const variant = inverse ? 'inverse' : 'light';` (`:32`). A third recipe variant is *unreachable from outside*. Adding `breadcrumb` also has to compose with `inverse` (a 4-way matrix), which a single boolean cannot express.
2. **Typography is nav typography, hard-coded in baseStyle.** `textStyle: 'navigation'` (`zimmNavItem.ts:17`) = `FONT_MEDIUM`, `fontSizes['3xs']` (12px), weight medium, `letterSpacings.sm`, **`textTransform: 'uppercase'`** (`foundation/typography.ts:211-218`) — plus a `fontFamily: 'var(--zimm-font-family-body)'` on the very next line (`:18`) that deliberately overrides the textStyle's family.
3. **The current crumb has no correct rendering.** Omitting `href` gives you a `<button>` (`:50-60`), which is wrong semantics for a non-interactive current page. There is no "render as plain text/`<span>`" path.
4. **No separator, no list wrapper, no `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">`/`<ol>`** — those belong to a parent, not this atom.
5. Geometry is nav-row geometry: `minHeight: var(--zimm-scale-xl)` (24px), `paddingBlock: 4.5px`, `justifyContent`/`alignItems: center`.
6. There is a base SFCC `Breadcrumb` at `app/components/breadcrumb/index.jsx` with **no** Zimmermann override yet (`.claude/registry/components.md:15`), `Layout/` is the documented story category for it (`components.md:119`), and a recipe named `Breadcrumb` would **fail** `recipeGuards.test.ts:212`. It must be `ZimmBreadcrumb`.

**What a `breadcrumb` variant would need to add (INFERRED from the above — not read anywhere):**
- A real `variant?: 'nav' | 'breadcrumb'` prop, composed with `inverse` using the same string-concat pattern zimmButton already uses (`zimmButton/index.tsx:60`, `` `${variant}${inverse ? 'Inverse' : ''}` ``) → recipe variants `nav`/`navInverse`/`breadcrumb`/`breadcrumbInverse`, or a `defaultProps.variant` shuffle.
- In `zimmNavItem.ts`: a `textStyle` (or explicit fontSize/letterSpacing/`textTransform: 'none'`) override, a `minHeight`/`paddingBlock` reset, and an explicit decision on whether the `'& > span'` hover underline survives — note that removing it from a variant requires `_hover: { '& > span': { borderBottomColor: 'transparent' } }`, since the base rule sets `currentColor`.

# 8. Deliberate deviations from the repo's written rules — do not "fix" these

All of (a)–(f), (h), (i), (k), (l) are intentional and, except where noted, documented in-file.

**(a) Folder location is undocumented.** `.claude/rules/conventions.md:81-94` says "each component lives in its own folder under `overrides/app/components/`" and shows a **flat** `productTile/` example; `.claude/skills/new-component/SKILL.md:29` says `overrides/app/components/<componentName>/index.tsx`. The atoms live at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/<name>/`. I grepped `ui-kits` across `.claude`, `.docs`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github` — the **only** hits are the six auto-generated registry rows (`.claude/registry/components.md:83-88`). The atomic-design nesting is a convention this branch established, not a written rule.

**(b) No default export.** `new-component/SKILL.md:30` says "named export (`export function <ComponentName>`) plus default export". Every atom is `export const X = (…) => {}` with **no** default export and no `function` keyword. This satisfies `components.md:13` ("No default exports of anonymous functions") and contradicts the skill. Follow the code.

**(c) `storybook/test`, not `@storybook/test`.** `.claude/rules/testing.md:87` prescribes `from '@storybook/test'`. Every story uses `from 'storybook/test'`. Forced by Storybook 10.4.6 (`package.json:24-37`), which folded the test package into the root. Follow the code.

**(d) New raw-literal constants in recipes.** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:29-31` says "Never: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — … The one standing exception is `button.ts`'s provisional constants". This branch adds four more: `zimmNavItem.ts:11` `'4.5px'`, `zimmTextInput.ts:35` `'2.25rem'`, `zimmTextInput.ts:37` `0.4`, `zimmLogo/index.tsx:12-13` `'327px'`/`'39px'`. **Every one** is a named const preceded by a comment naming the missing token, the owner, and the sign-off state — and `zimmNavItem.ts:9-10` explicitly cites the precedent ("same provisional treatment as button.ts's BTN_PADDING_Y"). That comment form *is* the exception's admission ticket.

**(e) `zimmLogo` styles via raw inline `style`, bypassing the whole token hierarchy** (`overrideStyling.md:12-27`). Reason in-file: `index.tsx:15-19` (webpack `svg-sprite-loader`/`ignore-loader` prevent `<img src>` resolving an SVG import) and `:21-22` (an SVG `fill` needs a concrete value, not a `var()` reference — hence `useToken`).

**(f) `fontFamily` deliberately overriding `textStyle` on the very next line** — `zimmNavItem.ts:14-18`. Reads like a bug; the comment says it is not: "fontFamily below deliberately overrides it — Figma Default/Navigation binds brand/font/family/body, not the heading family textStyles.navigation carries."

**(g) `fontSize="l"` at `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302` is a REAL bug**, self-documented as an unfixed known offender at `recipeGuards.test.ts:29-32`. `l` is a `spacing` key, not a `fontSizes` key, so the declaration is dropped. Do not copy this shape.

**(h) Multipart recipes are hand-rolled.** No `defineMultiStyleConfig`/`createMultiStyleConfigHelpers`/`anatomy` anywhere in `overrides/app/theme` (verified by grep — only 4 hits, all `defineStyleConfig` in `button.ts` and `zimmNavItem.ts`). Multipart = plain `{ parts: [...], baseStyle }` object literal with a type-only Chakra import. Single-part = `defineStyleConfig`.

**(i) No co-located component test at all**, despite `testing.md:42` ("Components use `index.test.ts` next to `index.tsx`"). `new-component/SKILL.md:50` makes it optional ("only if the component owns non-trivial logic"), and this branch's answer to "non-trivial logic" is to move it out (hook / recipe resolver / util) and unit-test it there. `.claude/hooks/testFileRemind.sh` only reminds; it never blocks.

**(j) Magic-string recipe key — genuine, undocumented inconsistency.** `conventions.md:50-54` bans magic strings. `zimmNavItem/index.tsx:33` and `zimmTextInput/index.tsx:80` use inline literals; `footer/index.tsx:28` uses `const ZIMM_FOOTER_RECIPE = 'ZimmFooter';` across 5 call sites. The footer form is the one that matches the written rule. This is the one place I'd call an unresolved inconsistency rather than a documented deviation — pick the const form for new work.

**(k) `theme/components/` must not import from `foundation/` — but components may.** The convention is stated at `footer.ts:8-9`: "theme/components/ otherwise avoids direct foundation/ imports in favour of `--zimm-*` CSS vars. Breakpoints are a deliberate exception: media queries cannot consume var()." `zimmNavItem.ts` and `zimmTextInput.ts` hold to it perfectly — zero foundation imports, everything through `var()`. **Component files are the opposite:** `zimmIcon/index.tsx:2` imports `iconSizes` from `app/theme/foundation` directly, which is the explicitly sanctioned pattern per `theme/index.ts:41-45` and `foundation/sizes.ts:3-7` (those scales are deliberately not registered as Chakra scales, so they must be imported as constants).

**(l) Australian spelling in identifiers, American in DOM/Chakra props.** `conventions.md:44` mandates Australian. Honoured in `resolveBorderColour`/`resolveLabelColour`/`COLOUR_HALF_INV`/`foundation/colour.ts`; the React prop stays `color` (`zimmIcon/index.tsx:92`). Don't "correct" either side.

content.text:
## The sanitiser investigation — I overstated it, and here's the honest state

**What I verified.** jsdom *is* bundled into the production server output. `build/server-renderer.js` is **10.3 MB** and contains real jsdom internals — `implForWrapper`, `jsdomError`, the jsdom user-agent string. My earlier "jsdom isn't in the bundle" reading was wrong; I'd grepped line counts on a minified file where one line holds an enormous amount.

**What collapsed.** The crash trace points at `main-server.js:71360`. **That file does not exist in a production build** — the server bundles are `server-renderer.js` and `ssr.js`. `main-server.js` is the **dev-server** artifact. So the only observation of this crash comes from a `npm start` run in CI, not from a production build, and not from MRT.

**Where that leaves the mechanism.** `dist/index.mjs` does run `new JSDOM()` at module-evaluation time — that's read directly from the package. And a `__WEBPACK_DEFAULT_EXPORT__` TDZ error is exactly what you get when a module body throws partway through and never assigns its default binding, so a subsequent access to `.default` reports it as uninitialised. That's a coherent chain and it fits every symptom — PDP-only, SKU-independent, homepage fine.

**But I inferred it. I did not reproduce it.** I should have said so plainly the first time instead of presenting it as established.

So if SFCC-195 documents `isomorphic-dompurify` as the chosen approach, my "back it out" recommendation was premature. The right sequence is: reproduce it against a production server build, and only then decide. Two things worth knowing either way — **10 MB of jsdom in the SSR bundle is a real cold-start and memory cost** regardless of whether it crashes, and the crash can't be reproduced on MRT at all because pages don't server-render there.

I'd add one concrete check to the plan: build on `develop` and on our branch, and diff `server-renderer.js` size. That attributes the 10.3 MB properly instead of guessing.

Four more decisions — three are new, surfaced by the exploration.

You are settling ONE design-system question for the Frontend Development Lead. READ-ONLY: do not modify any repo file, do not commit, do not check out any branch (read other branches with `git show <ref>:<path>` / `git ls-tree`).

Repo: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa`, currently on `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-ui-static-product-information`.

## The question

**Is a breadcrumb crumb link a VARIANT of the existing `ZimmNavItem` atom, or a SEPARATE atom?**

The Lead's framing: "let's conduct further investigation on this by looking into PR 55, our goal is to determine whether the breadcrumbs are a separate atom or related to and a variant of the navItem atom."

This is a design-system question, so answer it from the design system's own logic, not from what is convenient to code. Give a clear recommendation.

## Primary source — PR #55, branch `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui`

Read in full:
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmNavItem/index.tsx` and `index.stories.tsx`
- `overrides/app/theme/components/zimmNavItem.ts`
- `overrides/app/theme/components/navConstants.ts`
- `overrides/app/theme/components/footer.ts` — specifically how the footer RESHAPES `ZimmNavItem` from outside via `sx` (look for `legalLink` and how `footer/index.tsx` passes it). This is the existing precedent for "same atom, different context" and it is the crux of the question.
- `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx` — every site where `ZimmNavItem` is used, and how each differs
- `overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts` — the `navigation` textStyle in full, and any other textStyle that a crumb might want instead

## Also weigh

1. **What the base SFCC breadcrumb does** — `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/breadcrumb/index.jsx` and its theme recipe at `app/theme/components/project/breadcrumb.js` (or wherever it lives — find it). What parts does base model? Does base treat a crumb as a link variant or as its own thing?
2. **What #57 built** — `overrides/app/components/breadcrumb/index.tsx` on the current branch. What styling did it actually need? Compare each style property it sets against what `ZimmNavItem` already provides, and produce a concrete diff: which properties match, which conflict, which are additional.
3. **The semantic difference.** A crumb trail's last item is the CURRENT PAGE — non-interactive, and correctly rendered as plain text with `aria-current="page"`, not as a link or a button. `ZimmNavItem` renders a `<button>` when no safe href is given. Assess how much that matters.
4. **Typography.** `textStyles.navigation` is uppercase, 12px, medium, letter-spacing sm. Is that what a crumb should be? Check the repo's textStyles for a better match, and note that the Figma spec for the PDP breadcrumb is currently MISSING (the Lead is sourcing a node reference separately) — so flag any conclusion that depends on it rather than guessing.
5. **The variant-composition problem.** `zimmNavItem/index.tsx` derives its recipe variant from a boolean: `const variant = inverse ? 'inverse' : 'light'`. A third variant is unreachable from outside. Note how `zimmButton/index.tsx` solves the same problem with string concatenation (`` `${variant}${inverse ? 'Inverse' : ''}` ``), and whether that pattern transfers.

Give a recommendation on a clear axis: **separate atom** / **variant of ZimmNavItem** / **something else** (e.g. a shared primitive both consume, or reuse-with-`sx` following the footer's `legalLink` precedent).

For your recommendation, specify concretely:
- The file(s) and their paths
- The props surface
- What the theme recipe holds, and its registered key name (remember `recipeGuards.test.ts` fails any non-`Zimm`-prefixed key that collides with a base SFCC recipe — and base DOES register `Breadcrumb`)
- What changes, if any, are needed to #55's files — and flag clearly that #55 is unmerged, so any change there is a coordination cost
- How the current-page item renders

Also state what the DESIGN SYSTEM would say if the two are genuinely the same component with different contexts — is there a Figma component-library signal either way that you can find in the repo (token names, `.zimm-*` classes in `globalStyles.ts`, existing story categories)?

## Rules
- Cite `path:line` for everything, and `git show <ref>:<path>` where you read another branch.
- Quote code and repo rules verbatim when you rely on them.
- Distinguish VERIFIED from inferred. Say plainly where the missing Figma design blocks a firm answer.
- Do not invent design values.

**1. What #55 actually did.** On `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui`:

- A recipe part is renamed so `styles.someName` becomes `undefined` — does anything fail, or does the element just render unstyled?

## Rules
- Cite `path:line`. Quote rules and code verbatim when relied on.

- Be even-handed: #55's pattern may well be better than the written rule. Say so if the evidence supports it.

content.text:
Now the name/price discussion — plainly, from the start.

## What's actually on screen, and who draws it

The PDP's right-hand column is drawn by one Salesforce component, `product-view` (1054 lines). Inside that file there's a small helper called `ProductViewHeader` at lines 63–99. It draws the product name and the price.

Two things about it matter:

**It's private.** It's declared inside that file and never exported, so nothing outside can import it, replace it, or wrap it.

**It's drawn twice** — once at line 584 for mobile, once at 643 for desktop. The responsive layout needs the name in two different places in the DOM, so there are two call sites, not one.

## Why we can't just restyle it

Chakra has two ways to set a style: a theme rule, or a direct prop written on the element. **Direct props always win.** Line 81 is `<Heading fontSize="2xl">` — a direct prop. So a perfect `Heading` recipe loses to it every time.

The tempting escape is to redefine what `2xl` means. It resolves through `theme.fontSizes`, which we don't register, so it currently falls through to Chakra's default 24px. We *could* register a scale and point `2xl` at the Figma value — but `2xl` is used across all of base SFCC, so we'd be changing type on every page to fix one heading. And that file is Tier 1. Dead end.

## Why we can't just draw ours above it

Our page can render anything it likes *around* `<ProductView>`. But `ProductView` always draws its own header — there's no prop to switch it off. So the name appears twice: ours and base's. Two headings, both read out by a screen reader.

We could CSS-hide base's. That's the option that looks like a shortcut and isn't: hidden-but-present content still reaches some assistive tech, the selector has to reach into another component's internals, and it breaks silently the next time Salesforce changes that markup.

And there's no slot to inject into. `ProductView` has exactly two — `imageGalleryFooter`, which renders under the gallery, and `customButtons`, which renders under the buttons. Neither is anywhere near the header.

## So there are really only two options

**Own a copy of `product-view` with one optional `renderHeader` prop**, defaulting to the existing private header. Cart, wishlist and the bonus-product modal pass nothing and get byte-identical output. Or **accept base's typography this sprint** and raise a follow-up.

## The thing that I think actually decides it

Both **SFCC-91 (colour swatches)** and **SFCC-92 (size selector and add-to-bag)** also live in that options column, and base already renders swatches and the CTA inside `product-view`. So they will each need to reach into the same file.

Which means a `product-view` override isn't a cost you're paying for name and price — **it's coming regardless, three times over.** The real choice is whether it gets built once, deliberately, with clean optional slots that default to base behaviour, or whether three tickets each work around its absence in their own way.

That reframes it from "fork 1054 lines to fix a font size" to "the PDP needs one shared seam, and this is the first ticket that hits it."

SFCC-89 uses the header slot; SFCC-91 and SFCC-92 get theirs ready-made. Cost: a 1054-line file to own and diff on every SFCC upgrade, landing in a path no tier list covers.

## Recommendation: override `product-view`, with a single header slot — not a speculative set

Here's the reasoning that decided it for me.

**The expensive part of overriding `product-view` is owning it, and that cost doesn't scale with slot count.** The moment the file exists in `overrides/`, you own 1054 lines and you diff them manually on every SFCC upgrade. Adding three slots instead of one saves you nothing on that. So the supposed economy of building SFCC-91's and SFCC-92's slots now is only a saving in review round-trips — which is the cheap part.

Meanwhile it buys real risk: **SFCC-91's swatches already exist in a different shape**, so a slot designed for them today would be designed against a component that's already been built another way. And `conventions.md` is explicit — *"resist speculative abstractions."*

**The actual diff is small.** One optional prop, defaulting to the existing private header. Roughly ten lines against a 1054-line file. Every other consumer passes nothing and gets byte-identical output.

**And it delivers ACs 1 and 2 properly.** I considered accepting base's typography and deferring, and rejected it — on a luxury fashion storefront the type *is* the product, and SFCC-732 exists specifically to check it. Shipping a known-wrong heading on the highest-intent page in the funnel to save ten lines is the wrong trade.

**One implementation detail that matters:** the header renders at two call sites, mobile and desktop. The slot has to be threaded through both, and our header component has to work in both layout contexts. That's the part most likely to be got subtly wrong, so it's worth an explicit test.

**What would change my mind:** if getting Squad B's sign-off on a `product-view` override will outrun the sprint, then shipping the other four ACs plus a follow-up ticket for name/price beats blocking the whole story. That's a scheduling question you can answer and I can't — which is exactly what the tiering question is really about.

Two agents are still working — the crumb-atom question and whether #55's test pattern is sound or a gap.

questions.question: The product-view override lands at overrides/app/components/product-view/ — a path in no tier list, though protectedFiles.md groups its siblings (product-tile, image-gallery, swatch-group, display-price) as Tier 2, Squad B owns / notify Squad A. How do we treat it?

options.label: Treat as Tier 2, notify Squad B before the PR (Recommended)
options.description: Consistent with how every sibling shared-product component is already classified. Telling Squad B up front is the specific thing that would have prevented the breadcrumb surprise. Raise a separate rules PR to add the path properly, but don't block on it.

options.label: Get the tier ruling first, then write code
options.description: Both squad leads add the path to a tier list before the first commit, so the review path is unambiguous throughout. Cost: puts a governance dependency on the critical path of a story that's already six days overdue.

options.label: Treat as untiered, raise the gap separately
options.description: Follows the letter of the rules — no tier listed means normal review. Cost: a component four surfaces consume gets a normal review, which is precisely the mechanism by which the PLP breadcrumb changed without anyone noticing.

- `AGENTS.md:151` — "a `.test.ts` **or** a story `play`"
- `new-component/SKILL.md:50` — "**Optional:** … **Skip otherwise.**"
- `code-quality/SKILL.md:95` — "a `*.test.ts` exists **OR** a `play` function exists"

`.claude/hooks/testFileRemind.sh:55` — prints and `exit 0`. **Reminds, never blocks.**

## Break scenarios — what actually holds

**Caught** (plays outperform a typical render test here — they assert real `rel`/`target` hardening, accessible-name suffixes, focus-trap wrap direction): `isSafeHref ? <a> : <span>` both directions; `showContactChannels &&` both directions; `submitState === 'idle'`; nav-item a/button branch; molecule→atom threading of `trailing`, `errorText`, `name`; a dropped `aria-label` on the contact anchor (axe `link-name` under `preview.tsx:36` `test:'error'`, **plus** the play).

**Not caught — the three real gaps:**
1. **Recipe-part rename (S1).** `footer.ts:48-83` declares 35 parts, `footer/index.tsx` reads 35, zero drift today — but **no `footer.test.ts` exists**, `theme/index.test.tsx` has no `parts` assertion, and `__css={undefined}` renders unstyled silently. `zimmTextInput.test.ts:81-84` has the guard shape, but comparing `parts` to `baseStyle` keys stays green if you rename *both*. Nothing asserts **parts ↔ consumer usage**.

Required checks on `develop` (VERIFIED via API): **`Storybook interaction & a11y tests`**, `Unit tests (Vitest)`, `Branch Target Check`. Sanitiser util → **`.test.ts` required** (every rejection case as a row). Tier 1 governance — needs Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead, cannot ride in a feature PR. Reword `:42-43` to say it is a **location** rule not an existence rule, and name the one positive case (external-data-shape mapping) where a co-located test is required. <result>Analysis complete. Full document at `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/plans/let-s-plan-for-it-unified-tiger-agent-a624538a728f3e864.md` (plan mode was active, so that was the only file I was permitted to write — the requested scratchpad path was not written). Read-only throughout; #55 was read via `git show origin/feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui:<path>`.

## Recommendation: SEPARATE — and the design system says so explicitly, not by inference

The handover component contract answers both halves of the question, and it says **neither a nav-item variant nor a crumb atom**.

**VERIFIED** (on `f2r-component-registry`, not HEAD):
- The handover inventory declares exactly **27 `zimm-*` elements. None is a breadcrumb.** `git grep -E "zimm-breadcrumb|zimm-crumb"` across all refs: zero hits.
- `f2r/02-design/specs/components/nav-item.md:22` — "`<zimm-nav-item>` … **Used exclusively within `<zimm-navigation>`** to render the main nav link set." Its contract entry has only `label` + `active`, `slots: []`, **no variant axis**. Zero `crumb` references anywhere in its spec.
- Breadcrumbs are a **slot** on `zimm-page-toolbar`. `zimm-contract.js:387`: `{name: "crumbs", description: "Breadcrumb navigation. Consumer provides a <nav aria-label='Breadcrumb'> with <a> links…"}`
- The handover's own `elements/page-toolbar/demo.html:21-24` uses **plain anchors plus a trailing `<span>`** for the current page — it had `zimm-nav-item` available and didn't use it.

The architecture already on your branch (`ZimmPageToolbar variant="breadcrumbs"` wrapping a standalone `Breadcrumb`) matches that contract exactly. The remaining work is styling-layer, not structural.

## Structural arguments that hold regardless of the missing Figma

1. **The two disagree on what `aria-current="page"` means.** `zimmNavItem.ts:50-52` couples it to a permanent decorative underline on a still-clickable `<a>`. In a crumb it marks the terminal **non-interactive** `<span>` (`breadcrumb/index.tsx:74`). A Chakra variant changes style only — it cannot change the element or remove interactivity.
2. **`ZimmNavItem`'s element choice is href-driven, not role-driven** (`index.tsx:35-51`): no safe href → `<button>`. For a crumb the correct fallback is `<span>`; a `<button>` announces "clickable" for where you already are (WCAG 4.1.2).
3. **No SPA routing.** `ZimmNavItem` emits `chakra.a href` with no `as`/`to` prop. Crumbs need `RouteLink` or every click is a full reload — straight at the ≤2s p75 LCP budget.
4. **`ZimmNavItem` is empirically a *footer* atom.** Exhaustive sweep of #55: only two real call sites, both in `footer/index.tsx` (`:386`, `:493`). The header **did not adopt it** — `header.ts:76-88` has its own treatment with `NAV_LETTER_SPACING = '0.02em'`, which `navConstants.ts:1-5` records as *disagreeing* with the token and "unresolved with the UI designer."
5. **The `legalLink` precedent argues against reuse once you read it.** `footer.ts:396-404` changes tokens (textStyle/colour/padding) and **keeps** the underline, the a/button fallback and the aria-current behaviour — legitimate same-behaviour/different-context. A crumb inverts that. It's the test the crumb fails, not the precedent it passes.
6. **zimmButton's concatenation transfers mechanically but costs speculative variants.** `${variant}${inverse ? 'Inverse' : ''}` (`zimmButton/index.tsx:60`) would give `light|inverse|crumbLight|crumbInverse` — two of which have no Figma. Against "don't guess at design values."

**Style diff:** 5 properties match (all of them just the shared tokens — 12px/500/ls-0/`text.default`/`textDecoration: none`), **4 conflict** (fontFamily, lineHeight 18px vs 14px, hover opacity vs underline, aria-current treatment), **9 unwanted extras** dragged in (`inline-flex`, `minHeight` 24px, `paddingBlock: 4.5px`, cursor, border resets, inner span). The `inline-flex` + 24px pair is actively hostile to #57's `display: inline` `<li>` layout.

## Concrete spec

- Keep `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/breadcrumb/index.tsx` at that path (it shadows the base module; `conventions.md` requires kebab-case for base-mirroring files). Do **not** move to `ui-kits/molecules/`.
- New `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/theme/components/zimmBreadcrumb.ts`, registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.
- **Recipe key must be `ZimmBreadcrumb`, not `Breadcrumb`** — base registers `Breadcrumb` (`node_modules/.../app/theme/index.js:38,89`) and `recipeGuards.test.ts:216` whitelists only `['Button','Header','ListMenu']`. (That test exists **only on #55**, so the guard won't fire on HEAD yet — follow it anyway; the deep-merge hazard is real regardless.)
- Parts: `list`/`item`/`link`/`separator`/`current` — deliberately not base's `container`/`icon`/`link`.
- Props surface: keep #57's `{categories: readonly BreadcrumbCategory[], currentPage?: string}`.
- Current-page item: keep exactly as #57 renders it — `<li>` → `<Text as="span" aria-current="page">`, no link, no button, no trailing separator.
- **Changes needed to #55: NONE.** Only a one-line merge in `theme/components/index.ts`. The variant route would need edits to #55's atom, recipe **and** stories — re-opening a PR that's CodeRabbit-cleared and waiting on code-owner approval. It also creates a hard sequencing dependency: `ZimmNavItem` imports `isSafeHref` from `app/utils/safeHref`, which **does not exist on HEAD** (verified — `overrides/app/utils/` has only `productData.ts`, `sfccImage.ts`).

## Two things worth acting on beyond the question asked

**1. Highest priority — #57 breaks the SFCC bridge pattern.** The base breadcrumb **is** a shared internal dependency: `product-view/index.jsx:45` and `product-list/partials/page-header.jsx:14` both import it, and neither is overridden, so both currently render #57's component. `overrideStyling.md:133-139` requires the default export stay a faithful port with Zimmermann styling behind a named export. #57 exports the same branded component as both (`:84-86`) and additionally **injects a hardcoded `Home` crumb** (`:54-56`) that will now appear on the **PLP**, drops `...rest`, drops `sf-breadcrumb`/`sf-crumb-item`, drops `useStyleConfig`, and swaps the `ChevronRightIcon` separator for `/`. Fold a default/named split into the same refactor.

*Correction to a concern I raised and then disproved:* #57's local `categoryUrlBuilder` does **not** drop a locale segment. Base's util at `node_modules/.../app/utils/url.js:90` is `(category) => encodeURI('/category/' + category.id)` — it ignores the `intl.locale` the base breadcrumb passes it. content.text:
Confirmed, and it's worth correcting because it's the premise of the whole plan: **PR #55 is closed.** The live footer PR is **#59**, same branch, head `ec9d161` — which is exactly where the local branch sits. So "when #55 merges" should read "when **#59** merges." SFCC-55 is the ticket; #59 is the PR. **Test strategy — settled.** #59's pattern is sound, and my premise was wrong: `testing.md:42` sits under *"Layer 1 — Vitest → File layout"*, so it's a **naming rule for a Vitest file if you write one**, not a mandate that one exists. Three other surfaces say so explicitly — `AGENTS.md:151` says *"a `.test.ts` **or** a story `play`"*, and the new-component skill says *"Optional… Skip otherwise."* Adopting it: sanitiser and recipe get real unit tests, atoms get stories only, the molecule gets a `play`. Two things that came out of it worth banking. **The required checks on `develop` are Storybook interaction & a11y, Vitest, and Branch Target Check** — so `play` and a11y genuinely block merge, which is what makes the pattern safe. And **on #59's current head, both test gates are recorded as SKIPPED** — green by skip, same trap as #57. ## On `modelFit` — what it actually is Luxury PDPs show a line like *"Model is 178cm and wears a size 8"* so a shopper can judge fit against a known body. SFCC stores product data as attributes; custom ones are prefixed `c_`. Two matter here: - **`c_sizeFit`** — a block of HTML about sizing and fit. It's the content for the *Size & Fit* accordion, which is SFCC-102, a different ticket. - **`c_modelFit`** — created by SFCC-26 specifically to hold the model line for the PDP. What #57 does is take `c_sizeFit` — the accordion's content — run a regular expression across its HTML hunting for `
  • Model is…
    • `, and extract the text. That's scraping: reading a field meant for something else and pattern-matching a fragment out of it. It breaks three ways. The pattern only matches a **bare** `
  • `, so any attribute defeats it. It matches the **English words** "Model is", so it returns nothing on the other ten locales. And if anyone reorders the accordion copy, the line silently disappears — no error, just absent. `c_modelFit` exists so the line is its own field: fetched directly, no parsing, works in every language. The catch is that SFCC-26 is only "ready to deploy to UAT," so the field may not be in the sandbox yet — which is why the scrape is there. It works *today*.

questions.question: Given that — what's our data contract for the model line?

options.label: Read c_modelFit, render nothing when absent (Recommended)
options.description: Codes the field SFCC-26 created for exactly this. The AC already requires rendering nothing when there's no model copy, so 'absent' is a supported state, not a failure. Shows nothing in the sandbox today, starts working the moment the attribute deploys, no rework and no removal ticket.

options.label: Read c_modelFit, fall back to scraping c_sizeFit
options.description: Copy visible in every environment immediately, so QA can see it now. Cost: keeps the English-only regex, which means the fallback is the live path on 10 of 11 locales — and fallbacks like this tend to outlive their removal tickets.

options.label: Descope the model line from this story
options.description: Cleanest boundary — nothing built against an unavailable field, and it returns when SFCC-26 lands. Cost: drops one of the six ACs, needs Jas to agree, and the atom gets built later anyway.

questions.question: The prose atom needs a sanitiser on day one, but the isomorphic-dompurify SSR crash is unproven — I inferred it and never reproduced it. What do we build with while that gets settled?

options.label: Build behind a thin wrapper util, decide the engine later (Recommended)
options.description: One sanitise() util that every call site imports. Start with whichever engine, and swapping it later is a one-file change instead of touching every component. Also gives the unit tests a stable target. Sidesteps the blocked decision without pre-empting it.

options.label: Use isomorphic-dompurify now, since SFCC-195 documents it
options.description: Follows the documented decision, and Jhoan's reading may well be right. Cost: if the crash is real, it surfaces the moment Integration fixes server-rendering — and it's already in package.json without Hard Rule #7 approval recorded.

options.label: Reproduce the crash first, build nothing until it's settled
options.description: Highest confidence, and the reproduction is maybe an hour's work against a local production server. Cost: blocks the prose atom, which is on the critical path for two of the six ACs.

questions.question: Fixing testing.md's wording so it matches AGENTS.md and the skills is Tier 1 governance and can't ride in a feature PR. When?

options.label: Separate rules PR, in parallel with the build (Recommended)
options.description: One-line clarification, doesn't block anything, and it stops the next developer hitting the same contradiction we just spent an agent resolving. Needs both squad leads plus the Integration lead, but the change is small enough to review in minutes.

options.label: Defer until after this story ships
options.description: Keeps focus entirely on delivery. Cost: the contradiction stays live, and anyone reviewing our PR can legitimately cite testing.md against our test shape.

options.label: Batch it with the other rules fixes
options.description: Bundle it with the missing overrides.md, the uikit-components.md gap, and the broken @storybook/test import into one governance PR. More efficient review. Cost: bigger PR, slower to land, and the @storybook/test one actively breaks people now.

questions.question: Branch name for the fresh build?

options.label: feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info
options.description: Matches the ticket and the convention, distinct from the existing feature/SFCC-89_pdp-ui-static-product-information so both can coexist locally without confusion.

options.label: feature/SFCC-89_pdp-product-info-rebuild
options.description: Says explicitly that this supersedes the earlier attempt, which makes the intent obvious to anyone browsing branches. Cost: 'rebuild' reads as a judgement on Jhoan's work in a permanent, public place.

options.label: feature/SFCC-89_pdp-atoms
options.description: Describes the atom-first approach rather than the ticket scope. Cost: diverges from the naming convention and the story-key-first pattern the repo uses everywhere else.

## Breadcrumb: separate, and the handover says so explicitly

**The handover declares 27 `zimm-*` elements. None of them is a breadcrumb.** A grep for `zimm-breadcrumb` or `zimm-crumb` across every ref returns nothing.

Where breadcrumbs actually live in the contract is a **slot on the page toolbar** — `zimm-contract.js:387` spells it out: *"Breadcrumb navigation. Consumer provides a `<nav aria-label='Breadcrumb'>` with `<a>` links…"* And the handover's own toolbar demo uses **plain anchors with a trailing `<span>`** for the current page. It had the nav atom available and chose not to use it.

So `ZimmPageToolbar variant="breadcrumbs"` wrapping a standalone breadcrumb is already the contract-correct shape. What's left is styling, not structure.

**Four structural reasons it holds even without the Figma:** `aria-current` means opposite things in the two components — a decorative underline on a still-clickable link versus a terminal non-interactive element. The nav atom picks its element from whether it has a safe href, so a crumb with no link becomes a `<button>` announcing "clickable" for the page you're already on. It emits a plain `<a>` with no router integration, so every crumb click would be a full page reload against a 2s LCP budget. And it's empirically a *footer* atom — two call sites, both in the footer; the header didn't adopt it.

The style overlap bears that out: 5 properties match, **4 conflict**, and 9 unwanted ones come along — `inline-flex` plus a 24px min-height that's actively hostile to inline `<li>` layout.

**Best part: zero changes to #59.** Just a one-line registration merge. The variant route would mean editing #59's atom, recipe *and* stories — reopening a CodeRabbit-cleared PR that's waiting on code-owner approval.

**Three separators are in play with nothing to arbitrate:** base uses a chevron, #57 uses `/`, and the only format on record anywhere — the search PRD, SPR-46 — uses `HOME > SEARCH RESULTS FOR '[QUERY]'`. Worth putting to the designer alongside the node request. There's also no Figma node for the toolbar *or* the nav atom, so neither side of this comparison has a signed-off source.

**One place I disagree with the agent.** It says keep the component at `components/breadcrumb/` and fix the PLP leak with a faithful-default/branded-named export split. That's a correct reading of the bridge pattern — but it only applies if we need to override base at all. We don't: we need a breadcrumb on the PDP, and SFCC-578 owns the shared one. Building `zimmBreadcrumb` fresh and **never shadowing the base module** means the PLP is untouched by construction rather than by careful export discipline. I'd take that.

Three explanations, then the decisions. --- ## 1. The model line, and why the field matters **On screen** it's one sentence under the description: *"Model is 178cm and wears a size 8."* It exists so a shopper can judge fit against a known body — on a luxury site it measurably reduces returns. **Where product data lives.** Salesforce stores each product as a bag of attributes. Standard ones have plain names (`name`, `price`). Custom ones Zimmermann added are prefixed `c_`. Two are relevant: - **`c_sizeFit`** — a block of HTML about sizing and fit. It's the *content of the Size & Fit accordion*, which is a different ticket (SFCC-102). - **`c_modelFit`** — created by SFCC-26 to hold the model line, and nothing else. **What #57 does is scrape.** It takes `c_sizeFit` — the accordion's HTML — and runs this over it: ``` /
  • \s*(Model is[^<]*?)\s*<\/li>/i ``` That means: find a list item, check the text starts with "Model is", pull it out. It's reading a field built for something else and pattern-matching a fragment out of the middle. **Three ways it silently fails.** Not crashes — silently returns nothing, so the line just isn't there: | PIM content | Result | |---|---| | `

    • ` | ✅ found | | `
  • Model is 178cm…
    • ` | ❌ any attribute defeats it | | `

content.text:
## What actually ships with #59

**Nine Vitest files, six of them new for the footer:**

| File | Tests | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| `useSubscribeModal.test.tsx` | 3 | modal open/close state |
| `useZimmTextInputState.test.ts` | 8 | controlled/uncontrolled input state |
| `recipeGuards.test.ts` | 5 | invariants across **every** registered recipe, automatically |
| `zimmTextInput.test.ts` | 14 | colour-cascade resolvers + parts↔baseStyle wiring |
| `fontFace.test.tsx` | 6 | font asset URL resolution across browser/SSR/Storybook |
| `safeHref.test.ts` | `test.each` tables | the href allow-list, acceptances and rejections |

Plus `useContentfulClient`, `useCountryConfig` and `theme/index.test.tsx` carried from develop.

**Seventy-six Storybook stories, 21 with `play` functions** — and the footer itself has 7. These aren't smoke tests. They assert:

- WhatsApp link carries `target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, and an accessible name including "opens in a new tab" — **security hardening and a11y**
- The **negative** case: internal links must *not* have `target` and must *not* carry that suffix
- The whole subscribe flow — type email → submit → dialog opens → fill first and last name → continue → dialog closes → error surfaces
- Body scroll lock while the dialog is open

**So the answer to your question:** the footer isn't lightly tested — it's tested at the layer where the behaviour lives. Every piece of extractable logic has a Vitest file. The component itself is driven like a user through `play`, which runs as a **required check** on `develop` alongside the a11y gate.

What it doesn't have is a Vitest file that renders the footer and asserts markup appeared. That's the least informative test you can write — it breaks on every markup change and catches almost nothing. The one genuine hole is the Contentful data mapping: if a field mis-keys and becomes an empty string, a `play` sees an element that rendered, just blank. That's the case worth a co-located test.

## Sanitiser reproduction — first result, and it's a real finding

**The Node entry is definitively in the production server bundle.** This is `isomorphic-dompurify/dist/index.mjs`, minified:

```js
new Proxy(e=>xe(e),{get(e,t){const n=ke[t];return"function"==typeof n?n.bind(ke):n},apply:(e,t,[n])=>xe(n)}),Be=_e;
```

That maps one-to-one onto the source's Proxy with its `get` and `apply` traps. And `jsdom` is a **production** dependency in the lockfile, pulled in by `isomorphic-dompurify`'s own dependency list.

So the module-scope `new JSDOM()` is compiled into `build/server-renderer.js`. **The mechanism is present in production, not just in dev.**

**But that still doesn't prove it throws** — and I want to be careful here, because there's a real chance it doesn't. jsdom is a Node library and webpack's node target keeps its requires intact, so bundling it usually works. If so, the TDZ error in that dev log has a different cause entirely and I've been chasing the wrong module.

Settling it needs the build served and `/product/*` requested — which is running a server, so it's the plan's first task rather than something I do mid-planning. I'll write it up as a concrete, falsifiable step: serve `build/`, request a valid and an invalid SKU, capture the server log. Either the trace names this module or it doesn't.

Verified, and this is the sharpest thing our sources have to say about it.

## Against the repo's own rules: #59 conforms

Three of four governing surfaces explicitly permit what it did:

- `AGENTS.md`: *"every logic-heavy feature needs a `.test.ts` **or** a story `play`"*
- `code-quality/SKILL.md:95`: *"a `*.test.ts` exists **OR** a `play` function exists"*
- `new-component/SKILL.md:50`: *"**Optional**… **Skip otherwise.**"*

And `testing.md`'s own stated logic points the same way — test *"where failure would be non-obvious or costly"*, and explicitly **don't** test *"one-line passthroughs."* Five presentational atoms that map props to markup are passthroughs.

The one rule #59 actually breaks is the opposite of the one I'd been citing: *"**Do not duplicate coverage across layers**"* — the focus-trap and `aria-modal` behaviour is asserted in both the hook test and the footer `play`.

## Against "prove it can fail": mostly passes, one exemplary case

`recipeGuards.test.ts:168-174` does something no other suite in this repo does — it guards its own vacuity:

```ts
// Every other test here asserts an empty offender list, which an empty input
// satisfies just as well as a clean one. Without this, deleting `components`
// would turn the whole file green.
expect(collect().length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
```

That's the bar, met explicitly. `fontFace` and `theme/index` clear it incidentally via exact-count assertions. The one cheap gap is `zimmTextInput.test.ts:81`, which compares the recipe's `parts` array to its `baseStyle` keys — rename both sides and it stays green.

## Three holes, and none is closed by writing a component test

**Caught:** safe/unsafe href in both directions · the contact-channel conditional in both directions · submit state · the nav anchor/button branch · prop threading from molecule down to atom · a dropped `aria-label` (axe *and* the play).

**Not caught:**
- **Recipe-part rename.** `__css={undefined}` renders unstyled — silently. There's no `footer.test.ts`, and nothing asserts that the parts the recipe declares are the parts the component actually reads.
- **Contentful mapping.** A mis-keyed field falls to `?? ''` and produces an empty element. Invisible to a `play`, invisible to axe. `testing.md:19` lists data mapping *first* among things worth testing — this is the one genuinely indefensible gap.
- **`inverse` threading**, four levels deep and purely visual. Same for `aria-current` on the nav item: no axe rule covers it, and the `Active` story asserts nothing.

## The thing that outranks all of it

**Both required test gates are `skipped` on #59's head.** Verified just now against `ec9d161`:

| Required check | Result on `ec9d161` |
|---|---|
| `Unit tests (Vitest)` | **skipped** |
| `Storybook interaction & a11y tests` | **skipped** |
| `🔴 Branch Target Check` | success |

Only the governance checks and Deploy Preview actually ran. And a skipped required check **satisfies** branch protection — it reads as green.

So #59 ships genuinely well-aimed tests, and **not one of them executed on the commit that's awaiting your approval.** Same mechanism as #57: the last push touched only registry and script files, which fall outside every path allow-list, so `detect-changes` skipped the suites.

That's the real answer to your question. The testing that #59 ships is sound in design and unproven in fact — not because the tests are weak, but because nothing ran them where it counts.

You were right, and my claim was wrong in a way worth being precise about.

## The correction

`a207b9a` is the **last commit on #59 that touched `overrides/app/**`**. On that commit:

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `Unit tests (Vitest)` | **success** |
| `Storybook interaction & a11y tests` | **success** |

The two commits after it touched only `.claude/registry/components.md` and `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` — a generated doc and a build script, neither covered by any Vitest or Storybook test. So the skips aren't a hole; **they're the allow-list working correctly.** Nothing testable changed, so nothing needed re-proving.

And across the PR, the gates ran on seven commits and **passed every time**. The many `none` entries are just intermediate commits within a push — GitHub only attaches checks to the tip of each push.

**So #59's tests ran and passed on the code as it stands.** My "not one of them executed on the commit awaiting approval" was technically true of the head SHA and substantively misleading, which makes it worse than simply wrong.

## The rule I should have applied

I'd been checking *"did the gates run on head?"* The right question is *"did the gates run on the last commit that changed testable source?"* A skip after a docs-or-tooling-only commit is correct. A skip after a source change is the actual failure condition — and **neither #59 nor #57 exhibits it.**

That also means my framing of #57's two green-with-skips runs on 20 Aug was the same overreach. The mechanism is real — a skipped required check does satisfy branch protection — but it only matters under that narrower condition, and I stated it as though any skip were evidence of nothing.

This is the second time today I've taken one signal and inflated it past what it supports, the dompurify crash being the first. Worth me holding that pattern in view for the rest of this.

**What survives from the test analysis** is the part that didn't depend on the skip claim: the three coverage holes are real — no assertion that a recipe's declared parts match what the component actually reads, no test tying the Contentful data shape to props, and `inverse` threading four levels deep with nothing checking it. `testing.md:19` ranks data mapping *first* among things worth testing, so that middle one is the one genuinely worth closing.

content.text:
## Final verdict: sound — and better than the rule it appears to break

**Grade: adopt it as the basis.** #59's testing layer is the strongest in this codebase, and stronger than #57's.

### Why it holds up

**It tests behaviour, not markup.** Logic is moved out of components and covered where it lives — form state in `useZimmTextInputState` (8 tests), the href allow-list in `safeHref` (`test.each` tables), the colour cascade in `zimmTextInput`'s exported resolvers (14 tests), font asset resolution in `fontFace` (6 tests), modal state in `useSubscribeModal` (3). Nine Vitest files, six new for the footer.

**The `play` functions assert things worth asserting.** Not "did it render" — the footer's seven check `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and `target="_blank"` on external links, an accessible name including *"opens in a new tab"*, the **negative** case that internal links carry neither, the full subscribe journey through dialog open → fill → continue → close → error, and body scroll lock while the dialog is up. That's security hardening, accessibility contract, and multi-step state.

**It gates on the right checks.** Required on `develop`: Storybook interaction & a11y, Vitest, Branch Target Check. So all 76 stories run through axe at `error` severity, and the 21 plays block merge. That's what makes a play-only component defensible rather than untested.

**It contains the only self-verifying suite in the repo.** `recipeGuards.test.ts` walks every registered recipe and guards its own vacuity — `expect(collect().length).toBeGreaterThan(0)`, with a comment noting that without it, deleting the recipe map would turn the file green. That's the "prove it can fail" bar, met explicitly, once, by this PR.

**And it ran.** Gates passed on seven commits including `a207b9a`, the last one to touch `overrides/`. The subsequent skips are the allow-list working — only a generated registry doc and a build script changed.

**The missing co-located component tests aren't a deviation.** `AGENTS.md` says *"a `.test.ts` **or** a story `play`"*; `code-quality` says *"exists **OR** a `play` function exists"*; the component skill says *"Optional… Skip otherwise."* Only `testing.md:42` reads otherwise, and it sits under *Layer 1 — Vitest → File layout* — it governs where a file goes, not whether one exists.

### The three real gaps

**One that matters:** nothing ties the Contentful data shape to props. A mis-keyed field falls through `?? ''` and renders an empty element — invisible to a `play`, which only sees that something rendered, and invisible to axe, which only flags nameless *interactive* elements. `testing.md:19` ranks data mapping **first** among things worth testing. This is the one genuine hole.

**One that's latent:** nothing asserts that the parts a recipe declares are the parts the component actually reads. Zero drift today — the footer declares 35 and reads 35 — but when it drifts, `__css={undefined}` renders unstyled and silently.

**One that's cosmetic:** `inverse` threads four levels deep with nothing checking it, and `aria-current` on the nav item has no assertion and no axe rule.

### Two small things to fix

`zimmTextInput.test.ts:81` compares the recipe's `parts` to its `baseStyle` keys — rename both sides and it stays green. And the focus-trap behaviour is asserted in **both** the hook test and the footer `play`, which breaks `testing.md:3`'s *"Do not duplicate coverage across layers."*

### What to carry into our build

The pattern, unchanged — logic out, `play` for behaviour, a11y as the safety net. Plus the one addition #59 lacks: **a co-located test wherever external data maps to props.** For SFCC-89 that's the product-to-props mapping, which is exactly where a wrong field silently becomes an empty string.

# SFCC-89 — PDP Static Product Information (clean rebuild)

## Context

SFCC-89 delivers the static information block on the PDP: product name, price, description,
style code, an optional "Model is…" line, and a breadcrumb. It is the foundational PDP story
and SFCC-91 (colour swatches) will rebase onto whatever it establishes.

An existing attempt, **PR #57** by JhoanDelaCruz, is open at `CHANGES_REQUESTED` with **no human
review** — all 8 reviews and 22 threads are CodeRabbit. Its component layer is genuinely the best
worked example of the house styling pattern in the repo. Its integration layer is not: it
registers `/product/:productId` ahead of the base routes, so merging it would remove add-to-bag,
swatches, quantity picker, recommendations, accordions, SEO tags and 404 handling from the live
PDP. It also shadows the shared SFCC breadcrumb, silently restyling the PLP.

**Decision: clean rebuild on a fresh branch.** #57 is read as a reference — not copied from, and
not cherry-picked. It stays open and closes as superseded once this delivers.

**Outcome:** SFCC-89's six acceptance criteria delivered on an atom-first structure matching the
pattern established by **PR #59** (the footer), with the base PDP fully intact.

---

## Decisions locked

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| 1 | Cut the branch from `develop` now; rebase when **#59** merges (fonts + ui-kits arrive with it) |
| 2 | Clean build. #57 is a reference to read, not a source to copy |
| 3 | Breadcrumb **in scope**, built as a Zimmermann component that **never shadows** the base SFCC module |
| 4 | Tier rule: **icons don't count** — an atom may render an icon and stay an atom |
| 5 | Model line reads **`c_modelFit`**, renders nothing when absent |
| 6 | Sanitiser engine undecided — **reproduce the SSR crash first** (Phase 0) |
| 7 | `product-view` gets **one** override with a **single optional `renderHeader` slot**, no speculative slots |
| 8 | Treat `overrides/app/components/product-view/` as **Tier 2**; notify Squad B before the PR |
| 9 | If Squad B sign-off outruns the sprint, proceed on the Tier 2 verified-approver path |
| 10 | Test shape: adopt #59's pattern **plus** the five gap closures below |
| 11 | PR #57 stays open, closes as superseded |

**Still open:** branch name · the Figma node for the breadcrumb (you are sourcing it) · when to
fix `testing.md`'s wording.

---

## Starting point

Cut from `origin/develop` (`cd68e97`). Verified state there: **no `ui-kits/`**, no
`pages/product-detail/`, `theme/components/` registers only `Button`/`Header`/`ListMenu`,
`utils/` holds only `sfccImage.ts`, no `static/fonts/`.

**After #59 merges** the baseline gains: five atoms (`zimmButton`, `zimmIcon`, `zimmLogo`,
`zimmNavItem`, `zimmTextInput`), one molecule (`zimmInputAction`), recipes `zimmNavItem.ts` /
`zimmTextInput.ts` / `footer.ts`, `theme/fontFace.tsx` + two `.woff2`, `utils/safeHref.ts`, and
`recipeGuards.test.ts`.

**Rebase conflict set** (verified): `.claude/registry/*.md` (regenerate, never merge),

SFCC-89 ("PDP UI — static product information") has an existing attempt on PR #57, authored by
Jhoan. Its component layer is genuinely good — `ZimmPdpProductInfo` is the best worked example of
the house styling pattern in the repo. Its integration layer is not: the page override takes over
`/product/:productId` and renders only a static panel, so merging it would remove add-to-bag,
swatches, quantity picker, recommendations, accordions, SEO tags and 404 handling from the live PDP.

The decision is to **build the story fresh** rather than repair that branch, taking PR #57 and
SFCC-91 as references to read rather than sources to copy. The reasons: copy-first was never done,
which is the single root cause of both the PDP capability loss and a silent PLP breadcrumb
regression; and the atom-first structure the team has settled on (established by PR #59) didn't
exist when #57 was written.

The intended outcome is SFCC-89's six acceptance criteria delivered on top of an untouched
out-of-the-box PDP, with reusable atoms that SFCC-91, SFCC-92 and SFCC-194 can import instead of
each rebuilding a product name and price.

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Branch from `develop` now**, rebase when PR #59 lands. Our four atoms don't overlap #59's five, so conflict risk is low. |

| 3 | **Atom-first.** Four atoms + one molecule under `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/`. |
| 4 | **Icons don't count toward tier** — an atom may render an icon and remain an atom. Matches `ZimmButton` as already shipped on #59. |
| 5 | **Breadcrumb is in scope**, built as a Zimmermann molecule that **never shadows** the base SFCC breadcrumb module. |
| 6 | **Model line reads `c_modelFit`** and renders nothing when absent. No `c_sizeFit` scraping. |
| 7 | **Sanitiser: reproduce the SSR crash before choosing an engine.** Build behind a thin wrapper either way. |
| 8 | **`product-view` gets one override with a single optional `renderHeader` prop**, defaulting to the existing private header. No speculative slots for SFCC-91/92. |
| 9 | **Treat `overrides/app/components/product-view/` as Tier 2**, notify Squad B before the PR. If sign-off outruns the sprint, proceed on the verified-approver path. |

''` and renders an empty element — invisible to `play` (something rendered) and to axe (only flags nameless *interactive* elements). `testing.md:19` ranks data mapping first. | A co-located test for the product-to-props mapping: every field, including the absent case, asserting the *right* field reached the *right* prop. |
