# SFCC-89 — PDP static product information, built fresh

**Planning session 2026-08-23.** Still in planning; nothing built, no branch cut.

---

## Context

SFCC-89 ("PDP UI — static product information") has an existing attempt on PR #57, authored by
Jhoan. Its component layer is genuinely good — `ZimmPdpProductInfo` is the best worked example of
the house styling pattern in the repo. Its integration layer is not: the page override takes over
`/product/:productId` and renders only a static panel, so merging it would remove add-to-bag,
swatches, quantity picker, recommendations, accordions, SEO tags and 404 handling from the live PDP.

The decision is to **build the story fresh** rather than repair that branch, taking PR #57 and
SFCC-91 as references to read rather than sources to copy. The reasons: copy-first was never done,
which is the single root cause of both the PDP capability loss and a silent PLP breadcrumb
regression; and the atom-first structure the team has settled on (established by PR #59) didn't
exist when #57 was written.

The intended outcome is SFCC-89's six acceptance criteria delivered on top of an untouched
out-of-the-box PDP, with reusable atoms that SFCC-91, SFCC-92 and SFCC-194 can import instead of
each rebuilding a product name and price.

---

## Decisions locked

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Branch from `develop` now**, rebase when PR #59 lands. Our four atoms don't overlap #59's five, so conflict risk is low. |
| 2 | **Clean build.** #57 and SFCC-91 are references to read so we don't build blindly — not sources to copy. |
| 3 | **Atom-first.** Four atoms + one molecule under `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/`. |
| 4 | **Icons don't count toward tier** — an atom may render an icon and remain an atom. Matches `ZimmButton` as already shipped on #59. |
| 5 | **Breadcrumb is in scope**, built as a Zimmermann molecule that **never shadows** the base SFCC breadcrumb module. |
| 6 | **Model line reads `c_modelFit`** and renders nothing when absent. No `c_sizeFit` scraping. |
| 7 | **Sanitiser: reproduce the SSR crash before choosing an engine — and this is a hard gate.** No component code starts until it resolves. Build behind a thin wrapper either way. |
| 8 | **`product-view` gets one override with a single optional `renderHeader` prop**, defaulting to the existing private header. No speculative slots for SFCC-91/92. |
| 9 | **Treat `overrides/app/components/product-view/` as Tier 2**, notify Squad B before the PR. If sign-off outruns the sprint, proceed on the verified-approver path. |
| 10 | **PR #57 stays open**, closed as superseded once ours delivers. |
| 11 | **Copy-first the PDP page.** Non-negotiable; this is the step whose absence caused #57's problems. |
| 12 | **Test shape follows PR #59**, plus the gap closures in the section below. |

### Still open

- **Branch name** — deferred.
- **Breadcrumb visual reference** — no Figma node exists for the PDP breadcrumb; a reference is
  being sourced. Three separators are in circulation (base uses a chevron, #57 uses `/`, and the
  search PRD's SPR-46 uses `>` with uppercase `HOME`) and nothing arbitrates. **Do not invent one.**
- **Name/price typography** depends on the `product-view` override landing.

### Deferred by decision

- **`testing.md`'s `:42` wording fix** — deferred until after this story ships. Consequence to be
  aware of: the line remains quotable against our test shape during review, so the PR body should
  state the layer choice and cite `AGENTS.md`'s "`.test.ts` **or** a story `play`" up front rather
  than waiting to be challenged.

---

## Test coverage requirements

PR #59's testing layer is the basis: move logic out of components into hooks, utils and exported
recipe resolvers, unit-test it there, and let Storybook `play` drive the component. This is sound —
`AGENTS.md`, `code-quality/SKILL.md` and `new-component/SKILL.md` all permit `.test.ts` **or**
`play`, and Storybook interaction + a11y are required checks on `develop`, so a play-only component
is genuinely gated.

**Its gaps are these, and this build must close them.**

| # | Gap in #59 | What we must do |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | **Nothing ties external data shape to props.** A mis-keyed field falls through `?? ''` and renders an empty element — invisible to `play` (something rendered) and to axe (only flags nameless *interactive* elements). `testing.md:19` ranks data mapping first. | A co-located test for the product-to-props mapping: every field, including the absent case, asserting the *right* field reached the *right* prop. |
| G2 | **Nothing asserts a recipe's declared `parts` match what the component reads.** Drift yields `__css={undefined}` and silently unstyled markup. | In the recipe's test, assert `parts` ⊇ the set of part names the component actually consumes. Comparing `parts` to `baseStyle` keys is not enough — renaming both sides stays green. |
| G3 | **Prop threading through composition levels is unchecked** (`inverse` in #59, four levels deep). | Assert any prop that crosses more than one composition boundary reaches the leaf, via `play` or the mapping test. |
| G4 | **Vacuity.** Suites that assert an empty offender list pass just as well on empty input. Only `recipeGuards.test.ts` guards this, deliberately. | Any suite of ours asserting "no offenders" carries a self-test proving it collected something. Copy `recipeGuards.test.ts:168-174`. |
| G5 | **Duplicate coverage across layers** — #59 asserts focus-trap behaviour in both a hook test and a `play`, against `testing.md:3`. | Pick one layer per behaviour and note the choice. |
| G6 | **Process:** a skipped required check satisfies branch protection. Correct when only docs/tooling changed; a real hole when source changed and the gates skipped. | Before requesting review, verify the gates ran on the **last commit that touched testable source** — not merely on head. |

Concretely, for this build: the **sanitiser util** and the **theme recipe** get real Vitest files;
the **four atoms** get stories only (they are prop-to-markup passthroughs, which `testing.md:23`
explicitly excludes); the **molecule** gets a `play`; and the **page's data mapping** gets the G1
co-located test.

content.text:
No — and thanks for stopping me. The **component structure** is settled; the **styling substrate** and the **design inputs** are not. Here's the honest state.

## Settled

Tier rule (icons don't count) · placement at `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules}/<camelCase>/` · the four atom names and their textStyles · the molecule composes only atoms · breadcrumb as a separate Zimmermann molecule that never shadows base · recipe keys must be `Zimm`-prefixed · `var()` correct on sizing props, bare keys on spacing props · the test shape and its six gap closures.

## Not settled — ours to decide

**1. Page-level layout has no pattern at all.** I just checked: **no page in this repo consumes a theme recipe.** So there's no precedent for where a page's grid, gutters and column widths live. #57 put raw `var(--zimm-scale-4500)` directly in JSX — which is the boundary violation we've already ruled against — and there's nothing showing the right answer. This is where #57's worst styling sits, and we'd be inventing the convention.

**2. `zimmPageToolbar` doesn't exist on our base.** It's on #57 and SFCC-91 only — not `develop`, not #59. If the breadcrumb needs a bar, we're rebuilding it from scratch and naming it.

**3. Probably two of the four atoms need recipes, not zero.** `zimmProductMeta` needs a tone variant to serve both model copy and style code. `zimmProductProse` may need the mobile inset. My "no recipe unless variants or state" line was too clean.

**4. The conditional-spacing pattern is unresolved.** #57 exports `SPACE_DESCRIPTION_TO_META` and `SPACE_MODEL_INFO_TO_STYLE_CODE` *from* the recipe so the component can apply them as props — because each collapses to zero when the following block is absent. It's clever and traceable, but it is still styling at the call site. Keep it, or express it in the recipe with sibling selectors?

**5. The gallery.** #57 renders a grey placeholder box. If we copy-first the page, base's real gallery is already there — so no placeholder, but then the column proportions need to match a design measured against a placeholder.

## Not settled — needs the designer

Three Figma nodes are in circulation and nobody has said which is canonical: `3087:15747` (the page), `5083:70358` (where the info column was measured), and `5804-170721` (what SFCC-732/733 actually cite). Beyond that: no breadcrumb design · the 218px column, 180px gap and 140px padding, two of which have **no named token** · six off-scale values · `FONT_REGULAR` vs `FONT_MEDIUM` for price and meta · `#000000` versus `text.default` on two labels · the 768–1279px band undesigned · and the separator itself, which if it's a chevron needs `ZimmIcon` from #59.

## Dependency

`ZimmIcon`, `ZimmNavItem`, `safeHref` and the fonts are all on #59 and unmerged.

content.text:
## ELI5: why page layout is awkward here

**Chakra gives you two places to put styles.**

Directly on the element:
```tsx
<Box display="grid" columnGap="m" />
```

Or in a **recipe** — a named block of styles registered in the theme, which a component then reads:
```tsx
const styles = useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmFooter', {});
<Box __css={styles.linkColumn} />
```

**Why the project has a rule about which.** The footer taught this the hard way: when the same component's styling lives in two places, the two drift and nothing catches it. So the rule became *one canonical styling surface per component*, and that surface is the recipe.

**Why pages don't fit.** A recipe is a Chakra *component* concept — you register it under a key and a component reads it by that key. A page isn't a Chakra component; it's whatever a route renders. Nothing stops a page calling `useMultiStyleConfig`, it's just that **no page in this repo ever has.** So there's no precedent pointing either way.

**What #57 did.** Put the values straight into JSX:
```tsx
columnGap={{ base: 0, md: 'var(--zimm-scale-4500)' }}
```
A raw CSS variable in a component file — the boundary we've ruled against. And two of these values (180px gap, 140px padding) have **no named token at all**, so they couldn't become bare keys even if we wanted.

**The two live options, as code.**

A recipe for the page:
```ts
// theme/components/zimmPdpLayout.ts
export const ZimmPdpLayout = {
  parts: ['grid', 'galleryColumn', 'infoColumn'],
  baseStyle: { grid: { display: 'grid', columnGap: {...} }, /* … */ },
};
```

Or named constants in the page:
```tsx
// 180px — Figma measures 179px; no named token exists (spacing.ts tops out at 160px).
// Owner: UI designer. See token-gaps list.
const GRID_COLUMN_GAP = 'var(--zimm-scale-4500)';
```

**My recommendation changed based on your last answer.** I was going to say the recipe. But you've just chosen *"named const + comment naming the owner"* as the interim policy for unresolved values — and that **is** the second option's mechanism. Using it for tokens and a recipe for layout would put the same class of value in two different places.

There's also a cleanliness argument: a "page layout recipe" isn't really a component recipe, it's using the recipe system as a style dictionary. That works, but it's off-label — and the genuinely on-label version, a two-column layout component with its own recipe, **is** the hero that SFCC-723 owns.

So: named constants in the page, each carrying its derivation and owner, with a note that SFCC-723 should absorb them into a proper organism when it builds the hero. It's consistent with what you just decided, it doesn't invent a convention we'd have to defend, and it doesn't build another squad's ticket.

content.text:
## Named constants — and it's not a compromise, it's what the hierarchy prescribes

Reading `overrideStyling.md`'s hierarchy literally settles it. Tier 3, the recipe tier, is scoped:

> *"A component's own theme config (`theme/components/<name>.ts`) for anything that needs to **vary by variant/size/state** and **isn't already a Chakra prop**"*

The PDP's layout values fail both halves. They vary by **breakpoint**, which isn't variant/size/state — and `display`, `gridTemplateColumns`, `columnGap`, `padding` and `aspectRatio` are all already Chakra props. So the recipe tier doesn't apply by its own terms.

The "one canonical styling surface" section confirms it — it's explicitly about *interactive* components: *"For an interactive component with existing Chakra support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme config is the single source of truth."* The reason given is that a static surface can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/`_focusVisible`. **A page grid has none of those states, so there's nothing for a recipe to protect.**

There's also a structural objection. `theme/components/index.ts` is the *component* recipe registry, and `recipeGuards.test.ts` walks its keys asserting component-recipe invariants. Registering a page there means the guard iterates a page as though it were a component — it would pass, but it's a category error that makes the registry mean two things.

So these belong at **tier 2** — semantic token strings on Chakra props — with the standing provisional exception for the values that have no token. Which is exactly the policy you just chose.

**Concretely, the six values:**

| Value | Treatment |
|---|---|
| Info column width (218px) | named const — no token exists |
| Column gap (180px) | named const — `spacing.ts` tops out at 160px |
| Desktop right padding (140px) | named const — no token |
| Mobile gutter (30px) | import `grid.containerPadding.base` — it's exactly 30px, and `grid` isn't a registered scale so it comes in as a constant, not a bare key |
| Top padding (16px) | bare key `m` — registered, resolves through `theme.space` |
| Gallery aspect ratio | plain ratio literal — not a token concern |

Three named constants, each carrying its measured value, the missing token name and the owner. Not six.

# SFCC-89 — PDP static product information, built fresh

**Planning session 2026-08-23.** Still in planning; nothing built, no branch cut.

---

## Context

SFCC-89 ("PDP UI — static product information") has an existing attempt on PR #57, authored by
Jhoan. Its component layer is genuinely good — `ZimmPdpProductInfo` is the best worked example of
the house styling pattern in the repo. Its integration layer is not: the page override takes over
`/product/:productId` and renders only a static panel, so merging it would remove add-to-bag,
swatches, quantity picker, recommendations, accordions, SEO tags and 404 handling from the live PDP.

The decision is to **build the story fresh** rather than repair that branch, taking PR #57 and
SFCC-91 as references to read rather than sources to copy. The reasons: copy-first was never done,
which is the single root cause of both the PDP capability loss and a silent PLP breadcrumb
regression; and the atom-first structure the team has settled on (established by PR #59) didn't
exist when #57 was written.

The intended outcome is SFCC-89's six acceptance criteria delivered on top of an untouched
out-of-the-box PDP, with reusable atoms that SFCC-91, SFCC-92 and SFCC-194 can import instead of
each rebuilding a product name and price.

---

## Decisions locked

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Branch from `develop` now**, rebase when PR #59 lands. Our four atoms don't overlap #59's five, so conflict risk is low. |
| 2 | **Clean build.** #57 and SFCC-91 are references to read so we don't build blindly — not sources to copy. |
| 3 | **Atom-first.** Four atoms + one molecule under `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/`. |
| 4 | **Icons don't count toward tier** — an atom may render an icon and remain an atom. Matches `ZimmButton` as already shipped on #59. |
| 5 | **Breadcrumb is in scope**, built as a Zimmermann molecule that **never shadows** the base SFCC breadcrumb module. |
| 6 | **Model line reads `c_modelFit`** and renders nothing when absent. No `c_sizeFit` scraping. |
| 7 | **Sanitiser: reproduce the SSR crash before choosing an engine — and this is a hard gate.** No component code starts until it resolves. Build behind a thin wrapper either way. |
| 8 | **`product-view` gets one override with a single optional `renderHeader` prop**, defaulting to the existing private header. No speculative slots for SFCC-91/92. |
| 9 | **Treat `overrides/app/components/product-view/` as Tier 2**, notify Squad B before the PR. If sign-off outruns the sprint, proceed on the verified-approver path. |
| 10 | **PR #57 stays open**, closed as superseded once ours delivers. |
| 11 | **Copy-first the PDP page.** Non-negotiable; this is the step whose absence caused #57's problems. |
| 12 | **Test shape follows PR #59**, plus the gap closures in the section below. |
| 13 | **Page layout uses Chakra props on the page, not a recipe.** `overrideStyling.md`'s recipe tier is scoped to values that "vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop" — layout geometry varies by *breakpoint* on props Chakra already has, so the tier doesn't apply. The "one canonical surface" rule is explicitly about *interactive* components, and a grid has no states to lose. Registering a page in `theme/components/index.ts` would also make `recipeGuards.test.ts` walk a page as a component. |
| 14 | **Unresolved values get a named const + comment** stating the measured value, the missing token, and the owner — the standing provisional exception, as used by `button.ts` and `zimmNavItem.ts`. |
| 15 | **`zimmPageToolbar` is rebuilt as an atom with a proper theme recipe** (both existing versions lack one). Read SFCC-91's leaner version before writing. |
| 16 | **Recipes only where a variant or state exists** — `zimmProductMeta` (tone variant) and `zimmProductProse` (mobile inset) get them; `zimmProductName` and `zimmProductPrice` do not, following `zimmIcon`/`zimmLogo`. |

### Still open

- **Branch name** — deferred.
- **Breadcrumb visual reference** — no Figma node exists for the PDP breadcrumb; a reference is
  being sourced. Three separators are in circulation (base uses a chevron, #57 uses `/`, and the
  search PRD's SPR-46 uses `>` with uppercase `HOME`) and nothing arbitrates. **Do not invent one.**
- **Name/price typography** depends on the `product-view` override landing.

### Deferred by decision

- **`testing.md`'s `:42` wording fix** — deferred until after this story ships. Consequence to be
  aware of: the line remains quotable against our test shape during review, so the PR body should
  state the layer choice and cite `AGENTS.md`'s "`.test.ts` **or** a story `play`" up front rather
  than waiting to be challenged.

---

## Test coverage requirements

PR #59's testing layer is the basis: move logic out of components into hooks, utils and exported
recipe resolvers, unit-test it there, and let Storybook `play` drive the component. This is sound —
`AGENTS.md`, `code-quality/SKILL.md` and `new-component/SKILL.md` all permit `.test.ts` **or**
`play`, and Storybook interaction + a11y are required checks on `develop`, so a play-only component
is genuinely gated.

**Its gaps are these, and this build must close them.**

| # | Gap in #59 | What we must do |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | **Nothing ties external data shape to props.** A mis-keyed field falls through `?? ''` and renders an empty element — invisible to `play` (something rendered) and to axe (only flags nameless *interactive* elements). `testing.md:19` ranks data mapping first. | A co-located test for the product-to-props mapping: every field, including the absent case, asserting the *right* field reached the *right* prop. |
| G2 | **Nothing asserts a recipe's declared `parts` match what the component reads.** Drift yields `__css={undefined}` and silently unstyled markup. | In the recipe's test, assert `parts` ⊇ the set of part names the component actually consumes. Comparing `parts` to `baseStyle` keys is not enough — renaming both sides stays green. |
| G3 | **Prop threading through composition levels is unchecked** (`inverse` in #59, four levels deep). | Assert any prop that crosses more than one composition boundary reaches the leaf, via `play` or the mapping test. |
| G4 | **Vacuity.** Suites that assert an empty offender list pass just as well on empty input. Only `recipeGuards.test.ts` guards this, deliberately. | Any suite of ours asserting "no offenders" carries a self-test proving it collected something. Copy `recipeGuards.test.ts:168-174`. |
| G5 | **Duplicate coverage across layers** — #59 asserts focus-trap behaviour in both a hook test and a `play`, against `testing.md:3`. | Pick one layer per behaviour and note the choice. |
| G6 | **Process:** a skipped required check satisfies branch protection. Correct when only docs/tooling changed; a real hole when source changed and the gates skipped. | Before requesting review, verify the gates ran on the **last commit that touched testable source** — not merely on head. |

Concretely, for this build: the **sanitiser util** and the **theme recipe** get real Vitest files;
the **four atoms** get stories only (they are prop-to-markup passthroughs, which `testing.md:23`
explicitly excludes); the **molecule** gets a `play`; and the **page's data mapping** gets the G1
co-located test.

---

## Build sequence

### Phase 0 — the gate. No component code until this resolves.

**Reproduce or refute the SSR crash.** Serve `build/` and request a valid and an invalid SKU;
capture the server log.

Verified so far: the `isomorphic-dompurify` Node entry *is* compiled into
`build/server-renderer.js` — its Proxy with `get`/`apply` traps is identifiable in the minified
output — and `jsdom` is a **production** dependency pulled in by that package. **Unverified: that it
actually throws.** The original trace names `main-server.js`, a **dev-server** artifact that does not
exist in a production build. jsdom is a Node library and webpack's node target keeps its requires
intact, so bundling it may well work fine — in which case the TDZ error has a different cause and
the module is innocent.

Falsifiable outcome: either the production server log names this module on a `/product/*` request,
or it does not.

- **If it throws:** the engine choice is forced, and Hard Rule #7 becomes a defect report to
  Integration rather than a permission request.
- **If it does not:** `isomorphic-dompurify` stands as SFCC-195 documents it, and the only remaining
  question is the 10 MB of jsdom on the SSR path — a cold-start cost, not a correctness one.

**In parallel (non-code, so not gated):** cut the branch from `develop`; notify Squad B about the
intended `product-view` override and the breadcrumb decision; send the designer batch (see Token
gaps).

### Phase 1 — copy-first, then stop

Copy base `pages/product-detail/index.jsx` → `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`, convert
to TypeScript, add the temporary marker log, and verify the **full** PDP still works: add-to-bag,
swatches, quantity, gallery, accordions, recommendations, SEO tags present in the served HTML, and a
bad SKU returning 404. Pause for testing before any functional change.

Same treatment for `components/product-view/` if the header slot is in this slice.

Everything after this point is additive, so capability cannot be lost.

### Phase 2 — atoms

Four atoms under `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/`, each `index.tsx` + `index.stories.tsx`,
**no recipe** unless it needs variants or interaction state — following `zimmIcon`/`zimmLogo` on #59,
whose whole spec is a `textStyle` plus a token.

| Atom | Spec |
|---|---|
| `zimmProductName` | `textStyle="heading3"` — an exact match to what SFCC-732 asserts |
| `zimmProductPrice` | `textStyle="price"`, pending the font-weight ruling |
| `zimmProductProse` | the sanitised-HTML boundary — one auditable place, since `semgrep.yml` enforces it |
| `zimmProductMeta` | `caption`, with a tone variant covering model copy and style code |

**Page layout values** — six in total, and only three are literals:

| Value | Treatment |
|---|---|
| Info column width (218px) | named const — no token exists |
| Column gap (180px) | named const — `spacing.ts` tops out at 160px |
| Desktop right padding (140px) | named const — no token |
| Mobile gutter (30px) | import `grid.containerPadding.base` (exactly 30px; `grid` is not a registered scale, so it arrives as a constant — **not** the 32px `2xl` token) |
| Top padding (16px) | bare key `m` — registered, resolves via `theme.space` |
| Gallery aspect ratio | plain ratio literal — not a token concern |

Note in the PR that SFCC-723 (`pdp/hero`) should absorb these into the hero organism when it builds.

### Phase 3 — molecule

`zimmProductInfo` composes those four atoms and nothing else. `zimmBreadcrumb` as a second molecule
once the visual reference lands — **never** at `overrides/app/components/breadcrumb/`, which shadows
the shared SFCC module the PLP renders.

### Phase 4 — integrate

Insert into the ported page, remove the copy-first markers, and name every base behaviour
deliberately changed in the PR body.

---

## Verification

**Mechanical** — none of these is CI-gated, so they are honour-system and must actually be run:
`npx tsc --noEmit` · `npm run lint` (expect 17 pre-existing Contentful errors; ours must add none) ·
`npx vitest run` · `npm run build` then `npm run test:max-file-size` (vendor sits at 95.4% of
budget, so watch the headroom, not the pass) · `npx test-storybook --ci` against a built Storybook,
which runs every story through axe at `error` severity.

**Parity — the check that actually matters.** Re-run the Phase 1 checklist against the finished
page and confirm nothing regressed: add-to-bag completes · a swatch selection changes the variant ·
the quantity picker works · the gallery renders (and image URLs go through `proxyImageUrl`, or they
403 for real shoppers) · accordions open · all three recommendation rails render · SEO tags are
present in the **served** HTML, not just the React tree · an unknown SKU returns **404**, not 200.

**Acceptance criteria**, each against live SFCC data: name · single full price in storefront
currency · description · style code (master style number, **not** `product.id`) · model copy present
when `c_modelFit` exists and *cleanly absent* when it does not · breadcrumb reflecting the category
path with each node navigating correctly.

**E2E** — gherkin-first, in order: draft the `.feature`, get Lead QA sign-off, **then** generate the
spec. Tag every test with `@pdp` and `@SFCC-89`. Note `qa.yml` has no `e2e_pdp` allow-list group, so
PDP changes trigger the full Playwright suite, and the spec needs a `.p0.` segment to be selectable
by the SIT gate — both live in Tier 1 files, so they are Integration's, not ours.

**Before requesting review** — per G6, confirm the gates ran on the last commit that touched
testable source, rather than trusting a green tick on head.

---

**Create:** `ui-kits/atoms/{zimmProductName,zimmProductPrice,zimmProductProse,zimmProductMeta}/` ·
`ui-kits/molecules/{zimmProductInfo,zimmBreadcrumb}/` ·

`pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (copy-first port) · `components/product-view/` (scoped override)

## plugin:figma:figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md

content.text:
Something's off, and it's worth naming precisely rather than guessing.

Your file key is correct — `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` is the same one used earlier. But through this MCP the file reads as a **single empty page**: one canvas named `-----`, width 0, height 0, no children. And both your node IDs come back not-found.

That's not the file content the earlier sweep saw. It found a page called `└– 🟢 PDP` with 67 children spanning roughly 108000 × 42000 px, in this same file.

The explanation is in the tool contracts: these tools read **the Figma desktop app's local state**, not the Figma API. `get_metadata`'s own description says *"for a node or page in the Figma desktop app."* So if the desktop app doesn't have that file open, the key resolves to a stub — which is what we're seeing, and it's the same root cause as the *"You currently have nothing selected"* errors that blocked `get_variable_defs` and `get_design_context` earlier today.

Two consequences worth being straight about: I can't currently verify either of your node IDs exists, so my earlier line about `7310-5977` being "directly comparable" to the `3087:15747` measurements was ahead of the evidence — I was reading the URL, not the file. And the earlier measurements came through a *different* MCP server that's since disconnected, which may have had a different access path to the same file.

This was very productive. The design system is authoritative and it changes things.

## The desktop layout is exact — and #57's values were right

| Element | Position | Width |
|---|---|---|
| Gallery `list` | x=0 | **902** |
| `pdp/product-content` | x=**1082** | **218** |

So the gap is `1082 − 902` = **180px exactly**, and the right margin is `1440 − 1300` = **140px exactly**.

That means `--zimm-scale-4500` (180px) and `--zimm-scale-3500` (140px) are **precisely correct** — they aren't token gaps needing a designer at all. My earlier "1px off, 2px off" reading came from the 179/142 measurements, which were imprecise. The design system gives clean numbers, and **218px for the info column is now confirmed a third time.**

## `pdp/hero` and `pdp/product-content` are both real DS components

`pdp/hero` has four variants (Desktop/Mobile × Default/Expanded), Desktop Default at 1440×3557.8 — which pins SFCC-723's scope exactly. `pdp/product-content` is 218×606 desktop, 402×622 mobile.

## The composition differs from #57 in a way that matters

```
Content Card and Colour Swatch (218×214)
├── Content (218×82)
│   ├── Badge                     [hidden]     → SFCC-132/225
│   ├── Product name + Wishlist (218×24)       → name capped at 180px,
│   │                                            wishlist at x=194 → SFCC-434
│   ├── Price          y=44
│   └── Description    y=73
└── Colour Options     y=126  (218×88)         → SFCC-91
Size selector          y=242  (218×24)         → SFCC-92
CTAs                   y=294  (218×92)         → Button 218×52 + Link 218×24
Drawer                 y=414  (218×120)        → SFCC-195/102
modelDescription       y=562
styleCode              y=598
```

**Model description and style code sit at the very bottom — after the accordions.** #57 renders them immediately below the description. So the static information isn't one contiguous block: name, price and description are at the top, model copy and style code are at the *end*, with three other tickets' components in between.

**That breaks the `zimmProductInfo` molecule as planned.** It can't wrap all five fields, because the design interleaves other components between them.

Two smaller finds: `styleCode` is **two text nodes side by side** — a label at x=0 and the value at x=61 — not one concatenated string as #57 renders it. And the vertical rhythm is now legible: **20px** within the text group (that's `spacing.l`, a real token), **28px** between major blocks, **44px** after the content group. So two of the "six off-scale values" now have clear meaning.

**One conflict to flag rather than resolve:** the Button instance here is **218×52**, which contradicts the earlier finding that the button measures 50px and vindicates `button.ts`'s provisional constant over `actionSizes`. This says 52, which supports `actionSizes.height.lg`. Two measurements, two answers — that goes to the designer.

**And the breadcrumb:** the design system has **no** breadcrumb component, no disclaimer component and no page-toolbar component. Only **"PLP Bar desktop"**, a component set — which is the same candidate found earlier and matches the handover's `crumbs` *slot*. So your disclaimer-banner reading looks right: both are content inside that bar.

content.text:
That's the right question, and it has a better answer than my instinct was giving.

## The deciding signal is in the Figma node types

Figma distinguishes three things, and the distinction is the designer's own decision about what is and isn't a component:

| Node type | Means | Code equivalent |
|---|---|---|
| `symbol` | a component definition (with variants) | a component |
| `instance` | a *reference* to a component defined elsewhere | a component |
| `frame` | a layout container — internal structure | **not** a component; belongs to its parent |
| `text` | a text node | text with a `textStyle` |

Read `pdp/product-content` through that lens and it tells us exactly what it considers a component:

**Instances — so components:** `Badge` · `Add to wishlist` · **`Price`** · `Colour Options` · `Size selector` · `Button` · `Link` · `Drawer`

**Frames — so not components:** `Content Card and Colour Swatch` · `Content` · `Product name and Wishlist` · `wrapper` · `Product description container` · `CTAs` · `modelDescriptionContainer` · `styleCode`

**So in SFCC-89's scope, the design system says exactly one thing is a component: `Price`.** Name, description, model copy and style code are text nodes inside layout frames — not components at all.

## The signal hierarchy

**1. The design system's component boundaries.** Strongest signal, because it's a decision someone actually made rather than one we're inferring. An instance means a component; a frame means layout.

**2. Reuse across contexts.** `Price` exists as its own component set with `state=Sale` / `state=Default`, so it's genuinely reused. Nothing else in scope is.

**3. Variants or state.** `Price` has two states. `Size selector` has four. Product name has none — and a component with no variants and no state has nothing for a recipe to hold.

**4. Code-specific reasons the design can't see.** This is where we're allowed to disagree with Figma. A sanitised-HTML boundary is a security surface that semgrep enforces — worth one auditable module even though the design treats it as text.

**5. Then classify what you built** using the repo's rule — atom renders no other project component, molecule renders only atoms, organism renders at least one molecule. That's for *naming* what exists, not for deciding what to create.

## Applying it — leaner than I proposed

I'd suggested four atoms. The evidence supports **two**:

- **`zimmProductPrice`** — an atom with a recipe. It's the one true component boundary in the design, it has variants, and SFCC-194 (was/now pricing) will reuse it.
- **`zimmProductProse`** — an atom justified by signal 4, not by the design. It's the sanitiser boundary and it's used twice, for description and model copy.

**Product name and style code aren't components.** Name is `textStyle="heading3"` on an element; style code is a label-and-value pair. Whatever composes them owns them.

content.text:
It is confusing, and some of that is my fault — I've been using "component" in two different senses in the same breath.

## Untangling "component"

Three different things wear that word:

| Sense | What it means | Useful for decomposition? |
|---|---|---|
| **Figma component** | Something the designer marked reusable. Appears as `symbol` (the definition) or `instance` (a usage). A `frame` is *not* one — it's just a box for layout. | Yes — as evidence |
| **React component** | Any function returning JSX | No — *everything* is one, including the page |
| **Repo "component"** | Anything under `overrides/app/components/` | No — that's a folder, not a concept |

When I said "only `Price` is a component," I meant the **Figma** sense. That was sloppy shorthand and it's the source of the confusion.

## Two separate questions, which I'd been blending

**Question 1: should this thing exist as its own file at all?**

That's decided by whether it has **its own reason to change**. Four triggers, any one is enough:

- **Used in more than one place** — so a change happens once, not twice
- **Has variants or states** — which means it needs a theme recipe, and a recipe needs a name to register under
- **Owns a rule that must live in one place** — the sanitiser is the example; semgrep enforces it, so it shouldn't be scattered
- **Has logic worth testing on its own** — currency formatting, a regex, a mapping

If none of those apply, it's just markup belonging to its parent. Making it a file adds a hop to trace through and buys nothing.

**Question 2: what do we call the things that do exist?**

*That's* where atom/molecule/organism comes in, and it's purely mechanical:

- **atom** — renders no other project component
- **molecule** — renders only atoms
- **organism** — renders at least one molecule

Plus your two rulings: icons don't count, and slotted children don't count.

**This is a naming rule, not a design rule.** It tells you what to call something after you've decided to build it. It never tells you what to build.

## Where Figma fits

The node types are **evidence for question 1**, not an answer to it. When a designer promotes something to a component, they're usually saying "this repeats" or "this has states" — which are two of the four triggers. That's why it's a strong signal.

But it's evidence, not law. A designer might make something a component for their own file tidiness, or fail to when they should have. We're allowed to disagree — and we do, on the prose atom.

## Applied to SFCC-89

| Thing | Figma says | Own file? | Why | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Price** | `instance` — a component set with Sale/Default | **Yes** | Has variants → needs a recipe. SFCC-194 reuses it | atom |
| **Prose** (description + model copy) | `text` in a frame | **Yes** | Carries the sanitiser call, used twice, semgrep-enforced. *We disagree with Figma here, deliberately* | atom |
| **Product name** | `text` in a frame | **No** | No variants, used once, no logic. It's `textStyle="heading3"` on an element | — |
| **Style code** | two `text` nodes in a frame | **No** | Same — a label and a value, nothing to reuse or vary | — |
| **Page toolbar** | not in the DS | **Yes** | Three variants (breadcrumbs / recently-viewed / section-title) → recipe → name | atom (slots don't count) |
| **Breadcrumb trail** | not in the DS | **Yes** | Owns the `<nav>`/`<ol>` semantics and separator logic | molecule if crumb links become an atom, otherwise atom |

And **`pdp/hero` is the organism** — it renders the gallery group plus the product-content group. That's SFCC-723's, not ours.

So the four-versus-two question resolves cleanly: **two atoms exist because they have reasons to change; name and style code don't because they don't.** It isn't a retreat from atom-first — it's atom-first applied honestly, where an atom is a genuinely shared unit rather than every visible element promoted to a file.

No. Substantially not, and this is the important one.

## What I invented

**No file on any branch defines atom, molecule, or organism.** Zero hits across `develop`, the footer branch, and both f2r branches. The single grep match in `uikit-components.md` is the word "molecule" used incidentally in a CSS note about image wrappers collapsing.

The tier rule — *"an atom renders no other project component; a molecule renders only atoms; an organism renders at least one molecule"* — **I wrote that into the decomposition agent's brief.** The agent applied it faithfully, it came back in a findings table, and it has been reading like a project convention ever since.

Worse: I then asked you to rule on *"do icons count toward tier?"* as though I were resolving an ambiguity in an existing rule. There was no rule. That's now decision #4 in the plan file, resting on nothing. And `ui-kits/` on #59 contains only `atoms/` and `molecules/` — no `organisms/` — so even the directory layout doesn't assert three tiers.

## What is actually grounded

The repo does have guidance, in its own vocabulary:

| Source | Says |
|---|---|
| `components.md:22` | *"The trigger is **shared consumption**, not line count alone."* |
| `components.md:25` | JSDoc required on *"Any component used by **≥2 callers** (shared components…)"* |
| `components.md:30` | *"**Leaf components used by a single page** don't need JSDoc"* |
| `components.md:105` | *"**Not required** for purely **internal sub-components** that only render inside one parent"* |
| `new-component/SKILL.md:50` | *"if the component **owns non-trivial logic**, also create `index.test.ts`. **Skip otherwise.**"* |

So the repo's real categories are **shared** (≥2 callers), **leaf** (one page), and **internal sub-component** (one parent) — not atoms and molecules. And three of my four triggers do hold up: shared consumption, ≥2 callers, non-trivial logic. The variants trigger holds indirectly through `overrideStyling.md`'s recipe tier; the sanitiser one through `conventions.md` and `semgrep.yml`.

**So the conclusion survives — two things deserve files, not four — but on the repo's evidence rather than on a taxonomy I made up.**

## And a third option I never put to you

`components.md:105` names a concrete pattern: **`productTile/priceRow.tsx`** — an internal sub-component that is a real file, co-located inside its parent's folder, with no story of its own. That sits between "its own atom under `ui-kits/`" and "inline markup in the page." I framed the choice as binary and it isn't.

content.text:
The design system answers half of it, and you're right about the other half.

**"Product Card" is its own design-system component**, alongside "Product Cards Large Mobile". So the name on a PLP tile lives inside `Product Card`, and the name on a PDP lives inside `pdp/product-content` — **two components, each with its own name inside it.** The designer did not factor "product name" out into something shared.

But that's evidence, not proof, and your challenge splits cleanly in two.

## Style code — my answer holds

A style code is a PDP-level detail. It isn't on tiles, in the cart, or in search results. One consumer, no variants, no logic. It's a label and a value. Not a component.

## Product name — your challenge lands

It genuinely does appear everywhere: PDP, PLP tiles, cart lines, wishlist, search results, order confirmation. That's real reuse, and "used in more than one place" is the first trigger I listed. So by my own rule it should be an atom.

The thing that decides it is **whether the presentation is the same, not whether the data is.** A PDP name is an `<h1>` at `heading3`. A card name is almost certainly a link at a smaller style, and semantically a heading inside a list item rather than the page's h1. If those differ, they aren't one component with variants — they're two presentations that happen to show the same field. An atom is a presentational unit, not a data field.

If they're actually identical, then it *should* be one atom, and the design system being under-factored is a DS gap rather than a signal to follow.

**I can't settle that right now.** Search gives me a component key but no node ID, so I can't read `Product Card`'s internals — same blocker as "PLP Bar desktop". And there's no `product-tile` override in the repo to compare against; the PLP currently renders base SFCC's tile.

**What the citable rule says meanwhile:** `conventions.md` — extract *"once the same pattern appears in two places."* SFCC-89 is the first place. The trigger is the second, and by then we'd know what varies instead of guessing the variant axis. That's also what *"resist speculative abstractions"* is pointing at.

So my honest position: **style code isn't a component, and product name is undecided pending one measurement.** Not "isn't an atom" — I overstated that.

content.text:
Three straight answers.

## What the gap is

We don't know whether a product name **looks the same** on a PDP as it does on a PLP tile.

- **On the PDP** we can see it: a `text` node inside a frame, capped at 180px with the wishlist beside it at x=194.
- **On a tile** it lives inside a separate design-system component, `Product Card`. We haven't read its text style, its element, or its width behaviour.

That's the whole gap: one comparison, same-or-different.

## Why it matters

Because it decides whether "product name" is **one thing or two**.

An atom is a *presentational* unit — a look. It isn't a data field. So "the product name appears on every page" is a statement about the **field**, not about a component. Two pages can show the same field with completely different presentation and share nothing.

- Same presentation → one shared atom, no variants
- Different presentation → two local elements that happen to display the same field

## What would determine it

Reading `Product Card`'s internals — which needs its node ID, via right-click → **Copy link to selection**. Base SFCC's `product-tile` would be a weaker proxy, since that's Salesforce's styling rather than Zimmermann's.

## The choice you actually need to make

Narrower than I've been making it sound. It's just:

**Do we build the name as its own file now, or as markup in the page now?**

And the costs are asymmetric:

| Choice | If it turns out wrong |
|---|---|
| Build it local now | Extract it later when the PLP needs it — a ~15 minute refactor, done with both call sites visible |
| Build it shared now | We've guessed a variant axis with no second consumer; the PLP either ignores it or forces an awkward variant |

So being wrong in one direction is cheap and in the other is annoying. Which is why `conventions.md` points at the cheap one — extract on the second occurrence, not the first.

**That means the measurement doesn't gate this week's work.** It changes what we *expect* to happen when the PLP ticket lands; it doesn't change what we build now. I'd been framing it as a blocker and it isn't — that's on me.

content.text:
Both questions resolved, and one of them overturns an earlier finding.

## `PLP Bar desktop` is not a breadcrumb

Its contents:

```
Category Bar Container (1310×24)
├── Inner Category Bar Container (438×9)
│   ├── VIEW ALL          [hidden]
│   └── Category Text ×5  at x=0, 102, 196, 318, 407
└── Sort By and Filters Container (198×24)
    ├── Filters Text · Sort By Text · Icons · divider
```

Five **sibling** category links plus sort and filter controls. That's a category nav bar, not a hierarchical crumb trail. The earlier investigation called it "the only candidate" for the breadcrumb — **it isn't a breadcrumb at all.**

And your disclaimer hypothesis: the two are separate components. `Banner Desktop` is 40px at the very top of the page, *above* Navigation. The bar sits mid-page at y=1659. Different components, different positions.

`7310:5977` still returns not-found with the Designs file loaded, so that node ID doesn't resolve — possibly mistyped, possibly deleted.

**So there is no breadcrumb design anywhere I can find** — not in the design system, not in `PLP Bar desktop`, not in the PLP page designs.

## Product name is not a shared atom — now with evidence

| | PDP | PLP card |
|---|---|---|
| Node | `text` in a `wrapper` frame | `text` named `product` |
| Width | **180** (wishlist beside it) | **212** (full card width) |
| Cap-height | **11** | **9** |

Both are text nodes, so those cap-heights are comparable *to each other* — and 11 vs 9 means **different font sizes.** Different size, different width constraint, different semantic role. Two presentations of one field, not one component.

**And price isn't shared either.** The PDP uses an *instance* of `pdp/price`; the card uses a plain frame containing a text node. So `zimmProductPrice` is justified by its own Sale/Default variants — not by cross-page reuse, which I'd claimed. Worth correcting.

## One thing validated

`PLP Bar desktop` appears at **98px and 53px**; `PLP Bar Mobile` at **102, 50 and 43**. Multiple heights means multiple variants — which independently confirms that `zimmPageToolbar` having three variants was right, and it's a genuinely reused component.

So the decomposition now rests on evidence rather than instinct: **two atoms** (`zimmProductPrice` for its variants, `zimmProductProse` for the sanitiser boundary), **one toolbar atom** with validated variants, and **name plus style code as PDP-local markup**.

Found the Disclaimer — and it's a real component, but there's no breadcrumb in it:

```
Disclaimer (1440×130, at y=6876)

    ├── Title  (320×22)

        ├── Text (600×26)

```

A title on the left, body text and a link on the right. So your instinct that the breadcrumb sat near a disclaimer was spatially reasonable — they're both low on the page — but they're separate components and the Disclaimer contains no crumbs.

## The search is now exhaustive enough to conclude

Nine places checked:

| Checked | Result |
|---|---|
| DS search: "breadcrumb" | no component |
| DS search: "disclaimer banner" | no match |
| DS search: "page toolbar" | no match |
| `pdp/product-content` internals | no breadcrumb |
| `pdp/hero` internals | no breadcrumb |
| `PLP Bar desktop` (98px) | category + sort/filter bar |
| `PLP Bar Mobile` (102px) | same, no separators |
| `Disclaimer` | title + body + link |
| `7310:5977`, `7310:9231`, `7314:22263` | don't resolve |

**There is no breadcrumb design in either Figma file.** That's not "I couldn't find it" — that's having checked the design system by name, both PDP components, both PLP bars at both breakpoints, and the disclaimer.

Which matters because it changes the basis of your earlier call. You put the breadcrumb in scope expecting to supply a reference; you've now supplied six and none contains one. Building it would mean inventing every visual decision — separator, casing, size, spacing, placement — on a component another squad owns, where three separators are already in circulation with nothing to arbitrate.

One incidental find worth keeping: the Disclaimer uses a **`Link` instance**, so a reusable Link component exists in the DS. If a breadcrumb does get designed, that's likely what its crumbs are built from — which would make the crumb link a reuse of `Link`, not a new atom.

content.text:
Found it. **`PLP Bar desktop` has a `Breadcrumbs Container` variant:**

```
PLP Bar desktop (1440×200) — in the archived PDP
└── Breadcrumbs Container (1310×8) at x=40, y=64
    └── "About Link" TEXT (1310×8)
```

This resolves the structural question properly, and it vindicates what #57 and SFCC-91 both built:

**Breadcrumbs are a variant of the page bar, not a separate component.** The same `PLP Bar desktop` component has a `Category Bar Container` variant (what the current PLP designs use) *and* a `Breadcrumbs Container` variant. That matches the handover contract's `crumbs` **slot** on `zimm-page-toolbar` exactly.

What the design actually specifies:

- Lives inside the page bar, **40px left inset** (same as the category variant's container)
- **One text node spanning the full 1310px** — not a list of crumb items with separator elements. So the `/` or `>` separators are literal characters in the string, not markup
- Cap-height **8**, the same as `modelDescription` and `styleCode` on the PDP — consistent with `caption` (12px), though cap-height alone isn't proof

## But the status is the problem, not the structure

It's in the **archive** section. And the *current* designs tell a consistent story against it: `pdp/hero` and `pdp/product-content` have no breadcrumb, and every current PLP bar instance (98, 53, 102, 50, 43px) uses the `Category Bar Container` variant. The breadcrumbs variant appears **only** in archived designs.

So there are two readings and I can't distinguish them from the file: either the breadcrumb was designed and then **deliberately retired**, or the archive is old work and it's still intended but not yet redrawn.

One caution about how finished this is — the text layer is named **"About Link"**, which isn't a breadcrumb label. That looks like a repurposed layer, so I'd treat its exact values as indicative rather than specified.

**What this changes:** we now know *how* to build it if it's in scope — bar variant, 40px inset, caption type, single text line, separators as characters. What we still don't know is *whether* it should exist, and that's a design and product call rather than a developer one.

questions.question: The breadcrumbs variant exists on the page-bar component but only appears in archived designs — every current design uses the category-bar variant instead. How do we treat that?

options.label: Build it — the AC is authoritative, the archive gives us the structure (Recommended)
options.description: AC-6 is a confirmed requirement and now has a design precedent: page-bar variant, 40px inset, caption-sized single text line. Build to that, flag the archived provenance in the PR, and note the values are indicative since the layer is named 'About Link'. Keeps AC-6 met without inventing structure.

options.label: Ask the designer whether it was retired before building
options.description: The archive-only status is genuinely ambiguous, and if it was deliberately removed we'd be reinstating something the designer cut. One question resolves it, and they owe a breadcrumb spec anyway for SFCC-578. Cost: a dependency on an already-overdue story.

options.label: Out of scope — hand to SFCC-578 with these findings
options.description: Squad B owns the shared PLP+PDP breadcrumb, and we've now done the discovery work for them: it's a bar variant, here are the measurements, here's the archived precedent. Cost: AC-6 unmet, needs re-scoping with Jas.

questions.question: Separately — the bar being a component with both a breadcrumbs and a category variant changes what zimmPageToolbar is. Does that affect its scope here?

options.label: Build only the breadcrumbs variant now (Recommended)
options.description: The toolbar atom gets one variant, the one SFCC-89 needs. The category-bar variant belongs to the PLP work, and recently-viewed/section-title to whichever ticket renders those. Smallest surface, and the recipe is trivially extensible when the others arrive.

options.label: Build all the variants the designs show
options.description: The bar demonstrably has category, breadcrumbs, and the various heights used for recently-viewed and section-title. Building them together means one coherent recipe rather than four accretions. Cost: three of the four have no consumer in this ticket — speculative work.

options.label: Don't build a toolbar — render the breadcrumb directly
options.description: If the breadcrumb is the only bar content we need, skip the wrapper. Cost: contradicts the design system's own structure, and the padding lands back in the page instead of a recipe.

**Found it.** And the answer is genuinely useful.

## The archived bar has a Breadcrumbs variant

`PLP Bar desktop` at 200px, in the archive:

```
Breadcrumbs Container (1310 × 8) at x=40, y=64
└── "About Link"  TEXT (1310 × 8)
```

And the **current** version of the same component at 123px:

```
Recently Viewed Container (1218 × 11) at x=40, y=80
└── "Recently Viewed Text" (145 × 11)
```

So `PLP Bar desktop` is **one multi-variant bar component**, and its variants across everything we've read are: **Breadcrumbs** (200px, archived) · **Recently Viewed** (123px) · **Category Bar** (98px, PLP) · a 53px section variant.

**That's exactly the three-variant shape `zimmPageToolbar` was built with.** #57 and SFCC-91 got that right, and the earlier conclusion that the breadcrumb is *content in a slotted bar* rather than a standalone component is confirmed by the design system itself.

## What we can and can't source

**Sourced:** it's a `breadcrumbs` variant of the bar · content inset **40px** from the page edge · **full-width single line** (1310 of 1440) · cap-height **8**, the smallest text size in play — the same as style code and mobile category text, so `caption`.

**Not sourced:** the content is **one text node named "About Link"** — a placeholder. There are no individual crumb nodes, so no separator character, no per-crumb treatment, no hover state, no current-page styling. The structure AC-6 describes (`HOME / NEW / DRESSES / [PRODUCT NAME]`) simply isn't drawn.

## And the part that matters most

**The current PDP designs don't use the Breadcrumbs variant at all.** `PDP 01` (`3093:67151`) is a complete desktop PDP with real copy, and it renders the bar twice — as Recently Viewed (123px) and the 53px variant. No breadcrumb.

So **AC-6 asks for something the current design has removed.** That's not a gap in our research; it's a genuine conflict between the ticket and the design, and it's exactly the kind of thing `AGENTS.md` says to surface rather than resolve silently.

Two other things that came out of that page, both worth banking:

**The 50-vs-52 button conflict is now explained.** `Button Large` in the composed PDP is **218×50**; the design-system `pdp/product-content` says **218×52**. Two different sources, two answers — so it's a real DS-versus-page inconsistency for the designer, not a measurement error.

**Style code is one text node in the composed page** — `"Style Code: 7300JS261"`, 191 wide — where the DS component splits it into a label and a value. So #57's concatenation matches the page and contradicts the component. Same class of inconsistency.

Fair — we went deep. Pulling all the way back.

## What we're doing and why

**Building SFCC-89 fresh** on a new branch rather than repairing PR #57. The reason: #57's component work is good, but its page override silently replaces the entire out-of-the-box PDP — merging it removes add-to-bag. That traces to one skipped step (copy-first), and rebuilding correctly is cleaner than unpicking it.

**Why this much planning:** you asked to attack it "as how it should be done… before we write a single piece of code." So we've been front-loading every decision that would otherwise get made badly mid-build.

## Already locked

Branch cut from `develop` now, rebase when #59 lands · clean build, #57 and SFCC-91 read as reference only · **copy-first the page**, non-negotiable · `product-view` gets one override with a single optional `renderHeader` prop, treated as Tier 2 with Squad B notified · model line reads `c_modelFit` and renders nothing when absent · layout values as Chakra props on the page, not a recipe · unresolved values get a named const plus an owner comment · test shape follows #59 plus six named gap closures · PR #57 stays open and closes as superseded · **the SSR crash reproduction is a hard gate** before any component code.

## What's actually left — three things

**1. Breadcrumb: in or out.** The evidence is now complete and it's a genuine conflict: AC-6 requires it, but the current PDP design doesn't render it, and the only version that exists is archived and is a single placeholder text node with no separator, no crumb structure, no states.

**2. The composing surface.** Does the page place the pieces directly, or do we build a container component mirroring `pdp/product-content`? I asked this earlier and we got diverted into the taxonomy discussion.

**3. Branch name.** Trivial, you deferred it.

## Effectively answered, just needs your nod

**Product name is PDP-local, not a shared atom.** You asked me to check Product Card before deciding — done: the PDP name is cap-height 11 at 180px wide, the card's is cap-height 9 at 212px. Different font sizes, different constraints. Two presentations of one field.

## Not our decisions

The designer owes: which node is canonical · button 50 vs 52 (DS says 52, composed page says 50) · the 28/44px gaps · `FONT_REGULAR` vs `FONT_MEDIUM` · the undesigned 768–1279 band · `body2Strong`'s letter-spacing · style code as one node or two. Integration owes the dependency ruling and the server-rendering finding. Squad B owes the `product-view` and breadcrumb-ownership nods.

Those are all logged in the plan with owners. They don't block us starting.

content.text:
Branch name and page-composes both locked. Here are the three answers you asked for.

## What the Figma findings point to

The **architecture is fully sourced**: the breadcrumb is a **variant of the bar component**, not a component of its own. `PLP Bar desktop` has four real variants across everything we read — Breadcrumbs (200px, archived), Recently Viewed (123px), Category Bar (98px), and a 53px section variant. The Breadcrumbs variant gives us a 40px page inset, a full-width single line, and caption-size text.

The **content is not sourced**: one placeholder text node named "About Link". No crumb nodes, so no separator, no casing, no states.

So we know the container precisely and the contents not at all.

## What #57 did

**Got two things right.** It built `zimmPageToolbar` with a `breadcrumbs` variant — which matches the Figma bar-variant architecture exactly. And it placed the breadcrumb at the bottom of the page, matching AC-6's "beneath the product pictures."

**Got two things wrong.** It put the component at `overrides/app/components/breadcrumb/`, which **shadows the shared SFCC module** — that's the path that silently restyled the PLP. And it invented every visual: `/` separator, uppercase, hardcoded "Home", no focus ring at all. It also made `categories` required, dropped `...rest` and `sf-crumb-item`, and got caught in a CodeRabbit loop over leaf categories that produced `Home/New/New/Product`.

## What #59 gives us

- **`utils/safeHref.ts`** — directly reusable for crumb hrefs. This is the real win.
- **The recipe shape** — `zimmNavItem.ts` as the single-part template, and the `Zimm` prefix discipline, which matters because base SFCC registers its own `Breadcrumb` recipe that would deep-merge.
- **`recipeGuards.test.ts`** — automatically enforces that prefix on any new recipe.
- **`.zimm-focus-visible`** — the focus treatment #57's crumb links lacked entirely.
- **The provisional-value comment convention** — a named const stating the measured value, the missing token and the owner. Exactly what three unsourced visuals need.

Note what we *don't* take: `zimmNavItem` itself. The earlier investigation established it's wrong for crumbs — its variant is derived from a boolean so a third is unreachable, its typography is uppercase nav, and it renders a `<button>` when there's no href where a crumb needs plain text.

## My recommendation — keep it, built narrow

I've shifted from "take it out." The reason: **the container is sourced and we're building the toolbar anyway.** Adding its `breadcrumbs` variant is small, and only three visual decisions are genuinely unsourced — separator, casing, hover. Those are exactly what the named-const-plus-owner-comment policy exists for.

Concretely: build the `breadcrumbs` variant on `zimmPageToolbar` from the sourced values, build the crumb trail as its own component that **never sits at `components/breadcrumb/`**, use `safeHref` and `.zimm-focus-visible` from #59, and put the three unsourced visuals in named consts. Raise the AC-versus-design conflict with Jas in parallel — on record, but not blocking.

That delivers AC-6, invents nothing silently, and avoids the PLP leak that was #57's actual defect.

content.text:
Both good questions, and the first one exposes something I'd been carrying without justifying.

## Why pageToolbar — honestly, we shouldn't build it

I kept it in the plan because #57 built it, not because SFCC-89 needs it. Checking that against our own rules:

`zimmPageToolbar` has four variants in Figma — Breadcrumbs, Recently Viewed, Category Bar, and a 53px section variant. **SFCC-89 has a consumer for exactly one of them.** The other three belong to other tickets, and #57's own `recently-viewed` and `section-title` variants shipped with no consumer at all.

That's the same situation as the product name, and the same rule applies — `conventions.md`'s *"resist speculative abstractions"* and extract on the second use. So: **put the padding on the breadcrumb component itself now, and extract a shared bar when Recently Viewed or section titles actually arrive.** One fewer component, and the one we do build has a real consumer.

That drops it from the plan. Good catch.

## Where the breadcrumb actually goes

The archived design answers this. In that PDP the page ran:

```
Navigation (116) → Logo masthead (114)
  → PDP Cards (1170)              ← the hero: gallery + info column
  → PDP Hero image (1170)
  → PDP Cards Images (585)
  → PDP Cards Images (585)
  → PLP Bar 200  ← THE BREADCRUMB, at y=3510
  → PLP Bar 53
  → Products M Module (812)       ← recommendation rail
  → Lookbook
→ Recently Viewed → Footer
```

So it sits **after the entire product-image stack and before the first recommendation rail.** Which is literally what AC-6 says — *"underneath the product pictures."*

#57 put it at the very end of the page after the grid. Given #57's page has only a placeholder gallery, that lands in roughly the same relative spot — so its placement wasn't wrong, but in the **ported base page** (which has real imagery, then `RecommendedProducts` rails, then accordions) the insertion point needs to be explicit: after the image section, before the first rail.

## What's sourced about its styling

**40px horizontal inset is solid** — it's the desktop page gutter, and it's consistent across four separate components: the Category Bar container, the Recently Viewed container, the Disclaimer container, and the archived Breadcrumbs container. #57 used 40px horizontal too, which was right.

**Vertical padding is not sourced.** The archived bar is 200px tall with the text at y=64, which leaves 128px below — that bar was clearly sized for content it no longer holds, so its height tells us nothing. #57's 32px vertical (its most recent commit, in fact) was invented.

So: separator, casing, hover state, and vertical padding are the four unsourced values. Everything else has a source.

content.text:
That settles it, with real tokens. And it corrects several things I told you.

## The breadcrumb is fully sourced now

**Typography** — `Default/Caption-strong`: Futura Round body family, **12px**, weight **500**, line-height **18px**, letter-spacing **0**.

That is an **exact match to the repo's `textStyles.caption`** (`fontSizes['3xs']` 12px, `lineHeights['2xs']` 18px, `fontWeights.medium`, `letterSpacings.sm` = 0). So it's `textStyle="caption"` — no new token, no designer question.

**Spacing** — `alias/space/padding/1000` = **40px**, `alias/space/padding/800` = **32px**.

**So #57's "40px horizontal, 32px vertical" was correct on both axes.** I told you the vertical was invented. It's `padding/800`. That was its most recent commit and I mischaracterised it.

**Colour** — `text/default` `#191919`, on a `#f6f4f1` surface.

**Visual rules from the render** — separator `/` · **UPPERCASE** · terminal crumb is the product name with no trailing separator · wraps to two lines at 320px rather than truncating · crumbs are not underlined (only `READ MORE` is).

Only **hover state** remains genuinely unsourced.

## Three corrections to what I told you

**"No breadcrumb design exists anywhere."** Wrong. It exists in the current design. I checked nine places by reading node *names*, and the containing layer is named "Title" — so the tree hid it. A screenshot found it in one call. Lesson worth keeping: for "does this exist" questions, render it, don't grep the tree.

**"It's a variant of the PLP Bar."** That's the *archived* design. In the current design it moved into the **Disclaimer** component — the left column of a two-column bottom-of-page block, with disclaimer copy and a READ MORE link on the right.

**So `zimmPageToolbar` is definitively not needed.** Not for the breadcrumb, not for anything in SFCC-89. It's out of the plan for good.

## What this tells us — the substantive answer to your question

**The breadcrumb's real home is a shared bottom-of-page block, not a bar.** In code that's two components sitting in one row — a breadcrumb and a disclaimer block — because a crumb trail and legal/SEO copy have no semantic relationship. They're co-located for layout only. Building them as one component would be inheriting a Figma convenience as an architecture.

**And AC-6's placement is wrong.** It says *"beneath the product pictures."* The design puts it at the **bottom of the page, after the recommendation rails**, next to the disclaimer copy. That's a genuine ticket-versus-design discrepancy — and notably, **#57's placement at the bottom of the page matches the design better than the AC does.**

Which means #57 got the breadcrumb's placement, horizontal padding and vertical padding all right. Its actual defects were narrower than I've been saying: the shadowing path that leaked to the PLP, the missing focus ring, and the invented separator — and the separator turns out to be `/` anyway, so that one was right too.

content.text:
I read both in full. **Neither contains a breadcrumb** — and that's the answer.

## What's actually in those two designs

**`3093:67151` (PDP 01, desktop)** renders the bar twice, and I've now checked both instances: the 123px one at y=3510 and the 53px one at y=6421 are **both `Recently Viewed Container`**. So the earlier investigation's claim that `3093:67169` was "the only breadcrumb candidate" was wrong — it's Recently Viewed.

**`3093:67195` (PDP 01 Mob)** — full structure read: Navigation → Logo masthead → PDP Cards Mobile (carousel + info column) → Products Module → Large Product Card → bar (78) → hero image → Products Module → bar (50) → Recently Viewed → Footer. No breadcrumb at any position.

**And the Disclaimer isn't a breadcrumb.** It sits at y=6876 where the desktop Footer starts at y=6870 — so it's *inside* the Footer. Its contents are a `Title` (320×22), a `Body` with paragraph `Text` (600×26) and one `Link` (73×24). That's SEO footer copy. If it reads like a breadcrumb visually, it's a row of category links in an SEO block — same shape, different purpose.

## What that tells us

**The breadcrumb was deliberately removed.** It exists as a `Breadcrumbs Container` variant of the bar component — but only in the archive. Across the current desktop PDP, the current mobile PDP, the PLP designs, and the entire design system, it appears nowhere.

That's a much stronger finding than "we couldn't locate a design." A removal that's consistent across both breakpoints *and* absent from the design system is a design decision, not an oversight.

**So AC-6 is asking for something the design took out.** That's precisely the case `AGENTS.md` says to surface rather than resolve: *"If a user instruction contradicts either, pause immediately — cite the specific doc, section, and requirement ID."* Building it would mean implementing a component the designer removed, on the strength of a ticket that predates the current design.

I'm back to **out of scope** — but now for a defensible reason rather than an absence of evidence.

## Two things confirmed along the way

**Mobile gutters are 30px symmetric** — the info column sits at x=30, 342 wide, in a 402 frame. That's the third independent confirmation that `grid.containerPadding.base` (30px) is right and the 32px `2xl` token is wrong for that gutter.

**Both composed pages put `Button Large` at 50px** — 218×50 desktop, 342×50 mobile — against the design system's 52. So it's the DS component that's the outlier, not the pages. That reframes the designer question: it's not "which is right?" but "the DS component disagrees with every page that uses it."

## Where that leaves us

**Things that changed:**

- **The breadcrumb is fully designed** — separator, casing, format, width, gutter and vertical inset all sourced. It was never a design gap; it was a layer-name problem.
- **`zimmPageToolbar` is dropped entirely.** The breadcrumb doesn't sit in a bar; it's the left column of a Disclaimer band. Nothing in SFCC-89 needs a toolbar.

**The new question:** the breadcrumb's home is a band that also contains disclaimer copy and a `READ MORE` link — content that isn't SFCC-89's. And the band belongs, in Figma's structure, inside the Footer, which is Tier 2 and SFCC-55's territory.

content.text:
That resolves it, and it means my last conclusion was wrong too.

## The correction

SFCC-749 says the Disclaimer has three elements: a **left-aligned title** (*"e.g. TERMS AND CONDITIONS"*), a body paragraph, and a READ MORE link — **all three Contentful-driven, explicitly not hardcoded.**

So the node I read as "the breadcrumb, fully sourced" is the Disclaimer's **title field**, filled with breadcrumb-shaped placeholder copy. That's why it's a single text node named `Title`, why it wraps like prose rather than laying out as a nav, and why there are no individual crumb nodes.

And a breadcrumb **cannot** be that field. A breadcrumb is derived at runtime from the product's category path; the Disclaimer's title is authored in a CMS. They're structurally incompatible.

**So there is still no breadcrumb design.** Same conclusion I'd reached before, but now with a reason instead of an absence — and #57's `/` separator and uppercase turn out to have been copied from placeholder text in another component's title slot, not sourced from a spec.

I've now flipped on this four times in one session. Worth saying plainly so you weight my next assertion accordingly: I twice dismissed your disclaimer hypothesis from layer names, then over-corrected when the screenshot showed breadcrumb-shaped text, and your ticket search is what actually settled it.

## One caveat of yours I can close

You noted the extraction never enumerated the full PDP page, so absence isn't proof. **I did find the Disclaimer in the PDP** — it's the first child of the `Footer` instance (`3649:57311`), a 130px band above the footer proper. So it renders there exactly as SFCC-749 describes, as the shell component. That caveat is resolved.

## And the duplicate-scope pattern is now three deep

| Built / building | Duplicate ticket |
|---|---|
| SFCC-89 (this) | SFCC-737 `pdp/product-content` |
| SFCC-89's breadcrumb | SFCC-578 SEO Breadcrumb (Squad B) |
